Sports.title: Man United face defensive crisis with Lisandro Martinez missing training ahead of Champions League trip to Como... giving Michael Carrick a huge headache over who partners Harry Maguire
Sports.content:
Man United face defensive crisis with Lisandro Martinez missing training ahead of Champions League trip to Como... giving Michael Carrick a huge headache over who partners Harry Maguire

Manchester United are facing a defensive crisis on the eve of their crucial Champions League trip to face Como.

As the rain came down at Carrington, boss Michael Carrick observed a training session which featured just one senior centre back that has played this year in Harry Maguire.

Lisandro Martinez, who was forced off at half-time away at Leeds United with a thigh issue, was held back from Tuesday’s session, putting his selection for the trip to Como in doubt.

Leny Yoro sat the session out owing to his suspension after a red card in last week's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid. He is understood to be focusing on an individual training session today.

Ayden Heaven, who also missed the trip to Leeds through illness, was another defender absent from training, and he remains touch-and-go to be on this afternoon’s flight to Italy.

Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu remain longer term absentees, meaning Carrick is contending with five defensive injuries, all while Matthijs de Ligt, who did train, works his way back to full fitness having not played since November 2025.

Lisandro Martinez was forced off at half-time of United's 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday

Marcus Rashford came on in the closing stages of the game but did not train this morning

Marcus Rashford is another who is a major doubt to be on the flight as he continues to deal with a hip problem, which forced him to miss training.

Kobbie Mainoo has not played since the 1-1 draw at home to Tottenham Hotspur and he remains sidelined.

The big question now is who will be able to play in defence, especially given Carrick pivoted to a back five system for the 1-1 draw at Leeds.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui represent the only options at full-back - Harry Amass and Jaydan Kamason both trained with the first team but are unlikely to be called upon - while Maguire’s centre back partner is at this stage up in the air. Academy centre back Dan Armer, who was on the bench in Madrid, was also in the session.

United badly needed defensive reinforcements in the summer but dedicated their budget to bolstering the midfield following the sizeable exit of Casemiro.

That gamble not to bolster the back-line is coming home to roost now with the Como trip a major test of the squad depth with Carrick potentially needing to thrust De Ligt back into the mix after 11 months out.

Sports.title: Man United have a 'toxic culture', sparked by the 'Madrid' trio of Cristiano Ronaldo, Raphael Varane and Casemiro, claims ex-boss Erik ten Hag in damning breakdown of player discipline
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused the club's hierarchy of fueling a 'toxic culture'. Ten Hag, who was sacked in October 2024, has been forthright in his opinion of his former employers in a new interview with The Athletic, accusing the club of giving too much power to the players. The 56-year-old had a number of high-profile spats with members of his squad during his two years in charge, including with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho and Marcus Rashford. He has now claimed he was not supported by the club in sanctions on matters of player discipline, with Ten Hag wielding a reputation as an authoritarian during his time in charge. Rashford, for example, was left out of the Dutchman's starting line-up for a Premier League game against Wolves because he overslept and arrived late to a team meeting. 'And so, they (the club) are continuing the toxic culture; they fuel it, they give the power to the players,' Ten Hag told The Athletic. 'Rashford is an amazing player, if his mindset is right. I always showed my trust in him, played him. But when you show these standards, sometimes you have to make corrections.' Erik ten Hag had a number of high-profile spats with members of his squad during his two years in charge, the most high-profile with Cristiano Ronaldo In a new interview with The Athletic, the former Manchester United boss has claimed that the club's hierarchy have allowed player power to proliferate Ten Hag's most infamous spat came with Ronaldo, who claimed he had 'no respect' for the coach in a controversial interview with Piers Morgan in November 2022, which resulted in the Portugal forward's exit. In terms of Ronaldo's influence on the dressing room, Ten Hag said: 'Players have to act, they have a big responsibility. Football is, for some, not the highest priority. And United for some wasn’t the highest priority.' Ten Hag's comments are timely given it has been less than a week since Lisandro Martinez accused United's hierarchy of a lack of investment in the squad over the summer and said that he expected more from 'upstairs', singling out technical director Jason Wilcox. Despite refusing to comment on the Martinez situation, Ten Hag did accuse the former Real Madrid contingent – which included Ronaldo, Raphael Varane and Casemiro – of introducing a power imbalance. 'I can say I think that’s what the Madrid connection brought in, that players are powerful and they want to decide,' he said. 'In my opinion it didn’t suit the phase United was in. The leadership wanted attacking, dynamic football and these players wanted to play what fitted themselves.' Casemiro came to United as the midfield strategist with 'quarterback qualities', added Ten Hag. 'Then of course it looked like he got demotivated. I don’t know what they told him.' Player power has come under scrutiny on several occasions since Sir Alex Ferguson, an unyielding disciplinarian, departed the club in 2013. Ten Hag's successor Ruben Amorim was forced to wield the axe on several occasions after his players challenged his authority during his time at the reins. Ten Hag's comments come a week after Lisandro Martinez accused United's hierarchy of a lack of investment in the squad over the summer

Your browser does not support iframes.

Among them, Amorim claimed he would rather play his 63-year-old goalkeeper coach Jorge Vital in his team instead of Rashford unless the winger started to 'give the maximum every day in training and in life', a dispute which eventually led to the Englishman's departure away on loan to Aston Villa and Barcelona. Later, another academy graduate Alejandro Garnacho was told he could join a new club after he had questioned Amorim's call to drop him from the starting line-up of their Europa League final against Tottenham last year. Martinez, who publicly apologised for his comments last week, was handed a spot by Michael Carrick in the starting XI against Leeds at the weekend, where they could only manage a 1-1 draw. Despite former United captain Wayne Rooney claiming that Martinez's comments could rip the dressing room apart, Carrick has insisted that there is harmony. Ahead of the Leeds game, Carrick said: 'The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while actually. 'We're living it every day, we know what it feels like. We're emotional, we're passionate, we care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe they shouldn't say at a certain time, but that doesn't distract us from what we're creating here and the environment and the spirit within the group. 'It's not affected. I'm telling you as it is. We're in a good place, and I'm really happy.'

Sports.title: Dejan Kulusevski thanks Tottenham fans as star completes 'impossible journey' after 526-day absence with serious knee injury... and admits he told loved ones 'it might not work out' just two months ago
Sports.content:
Dejan Kulusevski completed his ‘impossible’ and ‘beautiful’ journey back to the Premier League and promised to repay Tottenham fans for their support in the difficult times. Kulusevski returned as an 87th-minute substitute on Monday. It was his first appearance since a serious knee injury in May 2025 and coincided with an upturn in fortunes for Spurs. Roberto De Zerbi’s strugglers beat Coventry 3-1 to secure their first league win of the season at the seventh attempt and climbed off the bottom of the table. James Maddison’s first goal for almost 18 months after his own injury nightmare and Kulusevski’s long-awaited return served to fuel the celebrations. 'The journey felt impossible,' said Kulusevski, 26. 'It was the most difficult it could be, but I had a feeling I was going to come back to play football. I just had to believe and that is what I do. 'I had to tell my closest ones it might not work out, just a couple of months ago. But in my heart, I always knew it would work out. I kept working. For 10 hours every day when no one is watching. Dejan Kulusevski has vowed to repay Tottenham fans support after making his first appearance in 526 days after a serious knee injury Kulusevski admitted the injury, sustained in May 2025 against Crystal Palace, led to him telling his loved ones a couple of months ago that his return might not work out 'Imagine when everyone gives up on you. And football for me is like breathing. Imagine you can’t breathe for two years but still you have a family, so you show up, you do it with a smile, you go with your team-mates, you hype them up and that takes a lot of love, a lot of courage and a lot of belief. That is what I had to practise. 'So, when everything was impossible and everyone gave up, I never gave up.' Kulusevski damaged a kneecap in a game against Crystal Palace. He had surgery but found he was still in pain and discomfort when he returned to training seven months later. There followed a course of injections and further rest and when that did not solve the problem he underwent another operation in March. It has been a long and difficult road with dire warnings about the delicate nature of the injury, and the popular Swede told how his Christian faith helped him through darker parts of his recovery. 'God, he gives me all the power,' said Kulusevski. 'I can’t take credit for what I’ve done because I haven’t done it alone. Every day he has been doing it for me. 'I will tell everyone about the journey. It has been an amazing journey even if it was hard sometimes. Hard is beautiful and I am so grateful that I had to experience it. 'Now I am ready to play football. I see myself a little different now. I think I am a different man now. Same guy, same guy that wants to play football but a little bit smarter.' Tottenham fans gave Kulusevski a rapturous ovation when he came on in the closing stages of their 3-1 victory over Coventry Spurs fans gave him a rapturous ovation as he peeled off his tracksuit to replace Mohamed Kudus. 'I am so grateful that they miss me play,' said Kulusevski. 'It means a lot and I am here to show them a better me. And a better me will be a better Spurs so we will be good.' He played in an internal practice match at the Tottenham training centre at the start of October and travelled with the squad but didn’t make the bench for the first game after the international break at Manchester United. By the time of the Coventry game, he was straining at the leash to get back on the pitch. 'I was more emotional in the morning,' said Kulusevski. 'I wasn’t nervous. I was ready to play those 10 minutes and make a good impact. It was amazing. It was fun. A beautiful day and I’m so happy we won.'

Sports.title: Crystal Palace's nightmare start to the season unpacked: The blunders that could cost Pierre Sage his job, how Steve Parish and Matt Hobbs sold him short in the transfer market - and why players feel worried and confused
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace's nightmare start to the season unpacked: The blunders that could cost Pierre Sage his job, how Steve Parish and Matt Hobbs sold him short in the transfer market - and why players feel worried and confused

Pierre Sage is understandably under intense scrutiny after Crystal Palace's shambolic 5-0 thrashing by rivals Brighton.

But that must not distract from the inexcusable failures of Sage's bosses, chairman Steve Parish and sporting director Matt Hobbs, who have failed to create the conditions for him to succeed over multiple transfer windows.

It does not absolve the Frenchman of blame. He is not helping himself with how he is setting his side up defensively. But it does provide important context to the conditions he is working under.

Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League, 17 in seven matches. And it is not as though they have been unlucky: they have faced the most shots and shots on target of any team, conceded a league-high 252 touches in their penalty area and have the highest expected goals (xG) against. They have been inviting teams to score – and repeatedly failing to do things as basic as winning headers and clearing their lines at corners.

Ultimately, that comes down to the manager and his tactics. Sage's emphasis on an intense press is leaving an already vulnerable Palace defence exposed. In his 3-4-3 formation, both wing-backs push into extraordinarily advanced positions and desert the back three. Under Oliver Glasner last season, one wing-back would hold a deeper position when Palace attacked, ensuring four defenders were in place to cover and react to transitions.

But now, the set-up is unbalanced – allowing teams to pick Palace apart quickly and attack their fragile backline. The midfield is not helping either, with Adam Wharton increasingly isolated as Quinten Timber marauds forward. There is too much focus on being front-footed and not enough caution with the personnel Sage has to choose from.

Pierre Sage is under serious pressure at Crystal Palace after a disappointing start to the Frenchman's tenure

Palace have looked shambolic at the back, especially in their 5-0 thrashing by Brighton (pictured)

Palace have frequently tried to play out in tight areas with the back three and Wharton while the rest of the team push forward, leaving them just one sloppy pass – of which there have been plenty – away from disaster.

Palace have taken seven points from seven games this season, matching Manchester United, and have won twice. In that respect, they are not yet in crisis. But both of their victories were fortuitous. Against Nottingham Forest, they should have been 5-0 down inside the first 40 minutes and rode their luck before punishing the visitors' profligacy.

Similar could be said about their victory at Fulham, where the hosts scored twice despite having 3.14 xG and Palace overperformed theirs with freakish goals. Their defensive performances have been consistently unconvincing, to say the least.

Sources at the club have echoed that view, too. Some in the dressing room are concerned about the lack of control in games and have been left confused by Sage’s ideas. Questions have also been raised about whether Palace have done enough defensive work on the training pitch and been given enough instructions. Sage remains well-liked on a personal level, however.

Again, there is mitigation: Sage, who impressed in taking Lens to a historic second-place finish in Ligue 1 with a similar system last season, has been unable to field a consistent back three due to injuries and Axel Disasi’s suspension.

Perhaps he does not have the personnel to play how he wants at Palace, especially with a back three that lacks recovery pace to deal with counter attacks. But even if that is true, the onus is on the manager to be pragmatic and adapt. Aside from an anomaly at Leeds, where Palace kept a clean sheet and were solid defensively, there has been no sign of that.

Sage was fighting to save his job against Leeds, with Parish considering sacking him over Palace’s defensive vulnerability. Daily Mail Sport understands Parish and Sage met on the week of the game, and the Palace chairman urged his manager to concentrate on defending.

Sage's job is once again at risk and if Palace fail to improve against Besiktas on Thursday night, Parish may be forced to act. However, Sage’s saving grace could be the quick succession of fixtures, which would leave limited time to find a replacement.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (centre) must take some of the blame after appearing complacent about the club leaving their business late in the transfer window

Sporting director Matt Hobbs has also failed to give Sage the conditions to succeed

HOW SAGE WAS SET UP TO FAIL

Sage has created plenty of problems for himself and his relative inexperience has done little to help him navigate adversity.

However, the root of the problem lies with errors made by the club’s hierarchy. Sage’s predecessor, Glasner, was brave enough to call out their deficiencies in several scathing press conferences. His public criticism raised eyebrows but it was never misplaced.

Glasner grew tired of inadequate transfer business and repeatedly scolded Parish for it. Sage does not seem the type to air his dirty laundry in public, although he surely holds a similar opinion behind closed doors.

Palace are paying the price for a lack of urgency in the summer window. Glasner criticised the club for two things: late transfer business and a failure to build a deep enough squad. In fairness, they addressed the latter ahead of their second European campaign, with options in each position. But the late panic buys continued, most damningly at centre back – the position where Palace most urgently needed to strengthen.

Two centre backs arrived after the season started, despite Palace selling England international Marc Guehi in January without a replacement and losing France international Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea during the World Cup.

Not only did those signings arrive too late, leaving Sage limited time to implement his ideas amid a hectic schedule, but both represented a significant downgrade. Palace received £72million for Guehi and Lacroix but replaced them with an 18-year-old loanee in Honest Ahanor and Chelsea cast-off Axel Disasi.

Disasi, to his credit, significantly improved West Ham’s defence in the second half of last season, albeit as a wide centre back. At Palace, he has been forced into the middle simply because they lack a natural option for the role. It is, quite frankly, poor squad planning.

Ahanor is an exciting prospect but remains a work in progress. With Palace also developing their own young centre back, Jaydee Canvot, their back three lacks the experience and proven quality required at this level, as the thumping at Brighton demonstrated.

Lacroix and Guehi lifted those around them, whether Canvot, Chris Richards or both. Palace no longer have that commanding, standards-raising figure and look feeble as a result. In fact, Takehiro Tomiyasu, signed as an understudy on a comparable wage to Nathaniel Clyne, who left the club in the summer, has been Palace’s best performer in the back three when available this season. He is now sidelined with injury.

Palace have lost two high-quality international centre backs this year, and replaced them with an 18-year-old loanee in Honest Ahanor (pictured) and a Chelsea cast-off in Axel Disasi

Youngster Jaydee Canvot (left) is among the defenders suffering from a lack of experience around him and Sage's bold set-up

Parish was naive when reviewing the club’s transfer business in an interview with The Athletic last month. Five of Palace’s summer signings arrived after the season began, four of them on deadline day, denying Sage vital time on the training ground in an already curtailed pre-season because of the World Cup.

Parish claimed the fact business was done late becomes irrelevant as the season progresses, but that disregards the difficult position it places the manager in to begin with. Particularly heading into a campaign in which Palace will be playing every three days for much of the season.

Parish said: ‘The important thing is that you get to the end of the transfer window and you say: “Have we done good business for the club?” We needed to make a bit of money on transfers, we needed to strengthen the squad in a different way with loans so that we had the squad depth but we weren’t necessarily carrying that cost going forward. In three months’ time, nobody cares if you did it early.’

The reality is Palace were hamstrung this summer because they overspent in January, splashing £83m on Brennan Johnson – a Glasner request – and Jorgen Strand Larsen. And those January signings were only necessary because Palace had failed to build a deep enough squad in the previous summer window. Consistently poor planning – it has consequences.

Hobbs and Parish took the importance of recruiting genuine quality at centre back far too lightly and are now paying the price. At some point, Sage will likely be the fall guy. But at least one of the Palace chiefs should take responsibility for their errors.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan accuses Erik ten Hag of LYING about Cristiano Ronaldo in furious response
Sports.content:
Piers Morgan accuses Erik ten Hag of LYING about Cristiano Ronaldo in furious response

Piers Morgan has issued a furious response to Erik ten Hag's comments on Cristiano Ronaldo after the Dutchman said he "let the team down" at Manchester United

View 2 Images Piers Morgan has accused Erik ten Hag of lying about Cristiano Ronaldo

Piers Morgan has accused Erik ten Hag of lying after the Dutchman claimed Cristiano Ronaldo "let the team down" and didn't train properly at Manchester United.

‌



‌



Ten Hag was appointed as United's new head coach in May 2022 and worked alongside Ronaldo during his brief homecoming at Old Trafford. But the pair would have a major falling out which led to the five-time Ballon d'Or winner having his contract terminated less than halfway through the 2022/23 season.

‌



And now, Ten Hag - who was sacked by United in November 2024 - has opened up on the issues he had with Ronaldo and alleged that he did not put the work in required by his manager and teammates.

‌



Speaking to The Athletic on Tuesday, Ten Hag said: "He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him. I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision."

After scoring 24 goals in 38 appearances for United in 2021/22, Ronaldo's second season was more challenging. Indeed, he struggled for form and Ten Hag has since claimed the Portugal international did not train hard enough when present, adding that he even "pulled out of training sessions".

‌



Ten Hag continued: "I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'.

View 2 Images Erik ten Hag and Cristiano Ronaldo had a fractured relationship at United (Image: Matthew Ashton - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



"He was not capable to do this. It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself.

"Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team. He was telling the players, 'Save your legs at training'. I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels."

‌



Ten Hag's comments caused quite the reaction on social media with Morgan among those to hit out at the ex-United head coach, and claimed he is NOT telling the truth.

"WHAT? This is a disgusting travesty of the truth," Morgan, who has a close relationship with Ronaldo, said on X.

‌



The broadcaster later added in a separate post: "REMINDER: Ten Hag went to Bayer Leverkusen after he was fired by United, and was fired again after just 62 days. No big club has gone near him since because…. he’s useless."

Ronaldo is still at Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr, where he has scored five goals in nine matches this season. He netted in last Monday's 3-1 win against Neftchi Fergana which has taken him to within 19 of the 1000-goal mark.

Sports.title: Elina Svitolina issues second statement as split hits Gael Monfils 'like a ton of bricks'
Sports.content:
Elina Svitolina issues second statement as split hits Gael Monfils 'like a ton of bricks'

Elina Svitolina has released another statement addressing her split from Gael Monfils after her husband recently announced his sudden retirement from tennis

View 3 Images Elina Svitolina has issued a fresh statement on her split from Gael Monfils

Elina Svitolina has issued a fresh statement to explain her separation from Gael Monfils further. The news is said to have hit her husband of five years and father of their daughter 'like a ton of bricks' after he abruptly retired earlier this month.

‌



‌



A joint social media post from Svitolina's perspective was released on Monday to announce they would be going their separate ways. The revelation came just days after news broke that Monfils had called time on his tennis career weeks earlier than expected.

‌



The Frenchman had already announced this year would be his last. However, he was scheduled to play two more tournaments.

‌



The first was this week's Lyon Open, followed by the forthcoming Paris Masters. However, he informed the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) of his retirement on October 5, bringing his career to an unexpected close.

At the time, the Lyon Open stated Monfils' withdrawal was down to "personal reasons". He also backed out of a pre-tournament exhibition match featuring other retired French players.

The 40-year-old has not publicly discussed his retirement, but Svitolina confirmed their marriage had ended on Monday in a shared Instagram post. The WTA number six has now published a second statement to "clarify" her earlier message.

‌



View 3 Images The tennis power announced on Monday their marriage had ended (Image: Simon Bruty, USTA via Getty Images)

Svitolina's most recent post also touches on Monfils' unexpected retirement, acknowledging that he chose to end his career due to their personal circumstances. Svitolina explained: "I just want to clarify my previous post a little, because I realised that not everyone, especially my international audience, fully understood what I was trying to say.

‌



"In that post, I shared only one of the reasons that influenced my decision and made me reflect on my life and my future. But the truth is, there's so much more to it, and it was never just about one thing.

"In many different situations, emotions, and difficult moments, you naturally start seeing life differently. Your perspective changes, your values and priorities shift, and you begin to understand what you truly want out of life.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"At some point, I simply realised that I didn't want to keep living a life where I wasn't truly happy. And believe me, coming to this decision was anything but easy.

‌



"I love and respect my husband very much. And I will always love and appreciate him for the person he is. That's exactly why it was so important for me to be honest, both with him and with myself."

The Ukrainian tennis ace also verified that they issued Monday's announcement to prevent any rumours surrounding Monfils' unexpected retirement. Despite being posted on both their Instagram profiles as a mutual statement, Svitolina clarified that it represented her version of their separation.

‌



View 3 Images Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils played together at the US Open (Image: AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)

She continued: "It's not always possible to explain everything behind such personal and difficult decisions in a single post. And honestly, some things are simply too personal to share publicly.

‌



"That was and is my view on announcing the end of our marriage but as some of you saw, Gael's career ended abruptly after he made the decision to stop based on our situation. Unfortunately he had many accusations thrown at him and he didn't deserve that, so we jointly released a statement.

"I just hope this helps you understand a little better what I was trying to say but please be kind and understanding, this is incredibly tough for us both right now."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Svitolina's fresh statement validates reports from L'Equipe that their separation came as somewhat of a bombshell to Monfils, prompting him to conclude his career prematurely. The French outlet said: "When Monfils learned the news, it hit him like a ton of bricks, and tennis, which he had often experienced as a kind of gentle madness, suddenly lost all meaning. He was no longer able to play."

Article continues below

This means that Monfils' last tournament was the US Open. The former world number six won his opening match on his 40th birthday before falling to Learner Tien in the second round.

Monfils and Svitolina, who share a four-year-old daughter, Skai, also partnered up to reach the semi-finals in mixed doubles.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan claims Chelsea 'bigger and worse offenders' than Man City
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan claims Chelsea 'bigger and worse offenders' than Man City

Simon Jordan has accused Chelsea of being 'bigger and worse offenders' than Manchester City, arguing the Blues continued breaking financial rules even after spending restrictions tightened

View 2 Images Simon Jordan has argued that Chelsea are bigger offenders than Manchester City

Simon Jordan has branded Chelsea 'bigger and worse offenders' than Manchester City, arguing the Blues broke financial rules despite benefiting from Roman Abramovich’s investment before tighter restrictions were introduced. His comments come after City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League.

‌



‌



City deny wrongdoing and have appealed against the ruling. Chelsea became one of English football's dominant forces after Abramovich bought the club from Ken Bates in 2003.

‌



His investment helped fund a team that won back-to-back Premier League titles under Jose Mourinho. The Blues won 21 trophies during Abramovich’s ownership, including five league titles and two Champions Leagues but later admitted breaches relating to undisclosed payments made during his tenure.

‌



Earlier this year, the club were hit with a £10.75million fine and given a suspended one-year first-team transfer ban over those violations. Chelsea also copped an immediate nine-month academy transfer ban and a separate £750,000 fine for breaches connected to youth player registrations.

Chelsea keeper Emi Martinez sends emotional message from hospital bed after surgery READ MORE :

Premier League announce fixture changes and TV picks including Arsenal vs Man Utd READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The financial violations centred on £47.5m worth of undisclosed payments made between 2011 and 2018 by third-party entities linked to Abramovich, for Chelsea's benefit. The Times reported that the payments were connected to deals involving Eden Hazard, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz, Andre Schurrle, Nemanja Matic and Samuel Eto'o, as well as three unnamed players.

‌



Payments were also reportedly made to former director of football Frank Arnesen and scout Piet de Visser. Chelsea's self-reporting and cooperation were taken into consideration when determining the penalties handed down.

The Premier League additionally concluded that the club would not have fallen foul of its profitability and sustainability rules even had the undisclosed payments been properly declared in their financial submissions. Jordan argued that Chelsea's early expenditure under Abramovich handed them a significant edge before financial restrictions were tightened.

‌



He believes their subsequent rule-breaking warrants far greater scrutiny, questioning why Manchester City have drawn considerably more fury. Speaking on Piers Morgan's Sports Uncensored, he said: "If you believe in fairness and Man City's team have been assembled in an unfair way, but the interesting thing for me is that if you introduce unjust rules - don't be surprised when people behave unjustly.

View 2 Images Chelsea enjoyed a hugely successful spell under former owner Roman Abramovich (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Why isn't there real rage about Chelsea? Chelsea were allowed to do what Man City were never allowed to do and yet, six years after they were allowed into the room, they still cheated.

"So Chelsea got in the room, got to spend what they want, Man City come along and then people went 'no, you can't come in, we're going to shut the door now.'

‌



"But Chelsea were already in that room and five years later, they're still cheating. So Chelsea actually are bigger offender and worse offenders than Man City. Because Man City weren't ever allowed to be in the room and they've had to cheat to get in the room.

"So when you think about it in those terms, start getting some ire about Chelsea as well."

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag slams Man Utd for breaking promises and 'embarrassing' Scott McTominay transfer
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag slams Man Utd for breaking promises and 'embarrassing' Scott McTominay transfer

Erik ten Hag has launched a scathing attack on Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Manchester United hierarchy in his first interview since being sacked as manager two years ago

View 3 Images Erik ten Hag has opened up about his exit from Manchester United (Image: Photo by Joris Verwijst/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

Erik ten Hag has accused the Manchester United hierarchy of breaking promises they made to him and says the sale of Scott McTominay left him "embarrassed".

‌



‌



The former United boss has launched a scathing attack on Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his Ineos team in his first major interview since being sacked by the club in October 2024. Ten Hag was dismissed months after signing a contract extension with United.

‌



The Dutchman won the FA Cup in May 2024 to add to his Carabao Cup from the previous campaign, but was still on shaky ground. United spoke with Thomas Tuchel and Roberto De Zerbi that summer before making a U-turn to trigger a clause in Ten Hag's contract to extend his stay.

‌



It was to prove a short-lived decision, with Ratcliffe and the United executives pulling the trigger to sack their manager following a dismal defeat by West Ham. Two years on from his dismissal, Ten Hag has opened up on what happened in an interview with The Athletic.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“I wouldn’t go on with only one year left,” he said. “So I said, ‘I need an extra year and we have to do it together’. They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.”

One of the promises Ten Hag says they made was to keep midfielder Scott McTominay, who had scored 10 goals in the 2024/25 season. However, United ended up selling the academy graduate to Napoli for £25million and the Scotland international has gone on to thrive in Italy.

‌



“That’s why I got disappointed,” Ten Hag said. “In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, ‘No selling Scott McTominay’. We would go aligned in the transfer window.

View 3 Images Erik ten Hag wanted to keep Scott McTominay (Image: Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"I make an argument, a reason: we don’t have scoring abilities. Scott brings scoring abilities and great mentality. He has United in all his veins. So when they bring up the subject, ‘No’. And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.”

‌



McTominay has 27 goals and 10 assists in 85 games for Napoli and helped the club win the Serie A title in his debut campaign. His transfer has been viewed as a major blunder by United, who used the funds to sign Manuel Ugarte for £50m from Paris Saint-Germain.

View 3 Images Frenkie de Jong was another failed target for Manchester United (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

‌



McTominay's exit wasn't the only transfer that left Ten Hag unhappy with those above him at Old Trafford. The former Ajax boss says he pushed for the signings of Frenkie de Jong, Declan Rice and Harry Kane.

Speaking about De Jong, he said: “Everyone’s thinking the manager is doing the negotiations, that I’m involved in financial issues, but I was never.

Article continues below

"Of course, I did my best; I set up meetings with him, where it was (former chief executive) Richard [Arnold] and (ex-football director) John [Murtough] involved as well, to pursue him to come over. He could have been very important building the team, not only that year but for the future. But we didn’t make it.”

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka row erupts as Graeme Souness calls Arsenal star a CHEAT in public attack
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka row erupts as Graeme Souness calls Arsenal star a CHEAT in public attack

Liverpool and Rangers legend Graeme Souness has hit out at Bukayo Saka and labelled him as a "cheat" in an astonishing attack after Arsenal's win at Nottingham Forest

View 2 Images Graeme Souness has slammed Bukayo Saka as a "cheat" (Image: @SportsUncensord/X)

Bukayo Saka is a "cheat" who "dives when he should be staying on his feet". That is the verdict of Graeme Souness, who has accused the Arsenal forward of "simulation" and deceiving referees without being fouled.

‌



‌



Souness made the comments during an explosive rant on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored. He argued that Saka goes to ground too easily and that Arsenal players put pressure on referees to influence their decisions.

‌



The Liverpool captain added that the England international, who is the second-most fouled player in the Premier League this season (21) behind Elliot Anderson (23), should remain on his feet rather than exaggerate contact.

‌



Saka faced criticism during a Champions League quarter-final tie against Bayern Munich in 2024 when he went down after receiving contact from Manuel Neuer, but referee Glenn Nyberg waved away appeals.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Now, Souness has slammed Saka after he was accused of diving again in Arsenal's 1-0 win against Nottingham Forest on Sunday, leaving Gunners fan Morgan incensed.

"Your man Saka dives all over the place. I don't want to hear about him. The minute he looks like losing possession, he's down," Souness said. "He simulates a foul. Anyone who simulates a foul in my book would be a cheat.

‌



"He dives when he should be staying on his feet. He's not alone. So Saka gets tackled, he screams as he's going down. The referee thinks there's nothing in that but wait a minute, he's stayed down. And then worse than that, everyone in the immediate area - all Arsenal players - put their hands up and scream foul.

View 2 Images Saka has been branded a "cheat" by Souness (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

‌



"The referee at that point panics and blows his whistle when it wasn't a foul - his first instinct was the right one. But he blows a foul because he's thinking, wait a minute, something I'm not understanding here.

"Simulation is a form of cheating, yes. But it's all over football today. If you asked 100 people what is it you dislike about the modern game, 50 per cent would say simulation, another 50 per cent would say VAR."

Article continues below

Saka and Arsenal are next in action when they travel to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. They then go up against Everton in the Premier League on Saturday before travelling to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup three days later. It's a chaotic period for the Gunners, who are facing six more matches in less than three weeks before the next international break.

Sports.title: Alex Scott whisked off on romantic trip by Jess Glynne days after leaving presenting role
Sports.content:
Alex Scott whisked off on romantic trip by Jess Glynne days after leaving presenting role

The England women's legend left the job just a month in after the show came in for criticism

View 2 Images Jess Glynne and Alex Scott during their recent holiday (Image: alexscott2/Instagram)

Alex Scott has moved on quickly after leaving her presenting role with Disney+ by enjoying a romantic getaway with girlfriend Jess Glynne. The England Lionesses legend recently stepped down from fronting Disney's coverage of the Women's Champions League after just two rounds of matches.

‌



‌



The show came in for criticism after technical problems led to an unscheduled advert break during Arsenal's game against HB Koge. The coverage, which included a dog with 137,000 Instagram followers, was also accused of undermining the women's game and being too "gimmicky."

‌



Addressing criticism of the coverage following her departure, Scott told the Observer : "Ultimately, do I agree with all the decisions that were made? Absolutely not. Did I try and advise? Yes, but I can only do so much.

‌



"But nobody sees the conversations, the fights I have behind the scenes. But I can hold my head up and know that I've always tried my best for the greater good of women's sport."

Alex Scott quits Disney+ job just weeks after new role began following BBC Football Focus exit READ MORE :

Scott, whose busy schedule includes fronting her own Women's Super League show on YouTube, has put her brief stint with Disney behind her by celebrating her 42nd with her singer-songwriter partner Glynne, who recently whisked her off to Paris.

With a reel of pictures and videos from the trip, which included a Celine Dion concert, Scott wrote on Instagram: "Another year older, another year bolder! Celebrating life in the beautiful city of Paris seeing the icon CÉLINE DION! A birthday experience that hit all the right notes...

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Thank you for every message, and every bit of love. My heart was full, my voice was LOUD, and my soul was HAPPY!! Paris, you were a dream….thank you @jessglynne ."

‌



It's been quite a year for Scott, who saw Football Focus, the show she'd presented since 2021, cancelled by the BBC after 52 years on air. She is now focusing on her YouTube show, One More Word WSL, which she launched via her own production company, First Cap Productions.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Addressing the new venture on social media last month, she said: "Four months ago, I quietly set up First Cap Productions. No big announcement, no funding, no team round a table, just an idea, built on something I've always believed: Stepping into your own power for the first time.

"Your first cap. Your first opportunity. Your first time finding your voice and being brave enough to use it. That's where First Cap came from. For the last four months I've been building a new show in the background, something I can't wait to share more information on with you soon.

‌



View 2 Images Scott during her brief stint on Disney+ (Image: Disney+)

"Then this past week I watched the women's football community explode with opinions, frustration, ideas and passion and I thought: this is exactly why I started First Cap."

Article continues below

Without Scott, Disney's Women's Champions League coverage, which is produced by ESPN, resumes on October 28. Lianne Sanderson, Nedum Onuoha and Shebahn Aherne remain part of the presenting team, alongside commentators Jacqui Oatley and Vicki Sparks.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand tells Man Utd they made transfer mistake over 'incredible' Man City star
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand tells Man Utd they made transfer mistake over 'incredible' Man City star

Manchester United spent £155million to sign Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos this summer, but Rio Ferdinand thinks that money could have been better spent elsewhere

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand has been impressed by Ayyoub Bouaddi (Image: Rio Ferdinand Presents)

Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed a trick by pulling out of the race to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi in the summer transfer window. Bouaddi joined Manchester City from Lille in a £85million move and has begun to show his talents on the pitch.

‌



‌



The 19-year-old midfielder was one of the most sought after players in the summer after catching the eye for Lille and Morocco. After selling Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez and losing Bernardo Silva on a free transfer, City splashed out to sign Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez.

‌



They were competing alongside United for midfielders, with Michael Carrick's side bringing in Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos for a combined £155m. Ferdinand is worried that their recruitment could be shown up after watching Bouaddi star off the bench for City against Paris Saint-Germain last week.

‌



"Did you see when Ayyoub Bouaddi came on? This is why I was talking about him over the last year and during the summer transfer window," Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

"He came on and showed PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France. He turned 19 this month, right? His transfer fee is the same as Santos and Tielemans combined. Manchester United were in for him, 100 per cent, but the fee was just too much.

"Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, 'oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.' I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.

‌



"Man City have got that many games that then can share the load about. Because of his age you can just dip him in and out but sooner rather than later that’s not going to fly with him because he’s an incredible footballer. They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily."

View 2 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi cost Manchester City £85million (Image: Mark Cosgrove/Getty Images)

Bouaddi has been eased into action by City manager Enzo Maresca, who sang his praises before starting him alongside Mateo Kovacic in their 3-2 win over Ipswich on the weekend.

‌



"Ayyoub, first of all, is a fantastic player," said Maresca. "The good thing about Ayyoub is that when he's on the pitch he's also improving the ones around him and this is what top players do.

"The ones that move around them are better and with Ayyoub the feeling that I have is that all the players around him are better. There are players who playing alongside some players can be better."

Article continues below

Bouaddi will be in contention to start for City when they host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday night before travelling to face Aston Villa on Saturday in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Richarlison urges police to intervene as Brazilian politician 'steals' private island
Sports.content:
Richarlison urges police to intervene as Brazilian politician 'steals' private island

Richarlison has called on Brazilian federal police to investigate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro over the alleged unlawful takeover of his private island

View Image Richarlison gave his version of events on social media

Richarlison has called on Brazilian police to launch an investigation into Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, accusing him of seizing his private island. The Tottenham outcast has taken to social media to voice his claims, alleging that Bolsonaro took control of the island without making any payment.

‌



‌



The island, which was purchased during the Covid-19 pandemic, had attracted interest from a number of prospective buyers, Bolsonaro amongst them. However, Richarlison refused to sell it to him.

‌



In a video posted on social media setting out his version of events, Richarlison said: "Between 2020 and 2021, I bought the island. Several potential buyers then came forward, but I didn't want to sell it. Flavio Bolsonaro was among those interested. He even used a drone to film the island from above, and there's a video of it on his Instagram.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Roberto De Zerbi reveals he banned phones in an effort to change Tottenham's fortunes READ MORE :

Premier League announce fixture changes and TV picks including Arsenal vs Man Utd READ MORE :

"But I didn't want to sell the island to him and they took advantage of the situation in court. We were sorting out the paperwork (documentation for the island's ownership), and they said it would take months or even years to resolve.

"Flavio Bolsonaro and this guy Willian Tomas went there and, in 24 hours, took possession of the island. That's where the justice system failed.

‌



"Those guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know. I have no received a penny and I spent around R$ 10 million (around £1.5million) there and received nothing.

"I'm asking the federal police to help and investigate this properly because we want answers. I want to recover my money, not get the island back.

‌



"If I do get the money back, I'll donate part of it to a hospital in my hometown to help them. I just want what's rightfully mine, which I earned through hard work."

Richarlison also called on his supporters to demand answers from Bolsonaro ahead of the presidential run-off against Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, scheduled for Sunday, October 25.

It has been a challenging year for Richarlison, who was left out of Roberto De Zerbi's 25-man Premier League squad after being unable to engineer a departure from Tottenham during the summer transfer window.

The Brazilian also seemed to have a public disagreement with De Zerbi, posting on social media an article that suggested there had been a 'fight' between the forward and his boss.

Richarlison has since turned out for Spurs' Under-21s, netting twice in a 2-2 draw against Cheltenham Town in the Jersey Mike's Trophy, though the League Two outfit went on to prevail on penalties.

His sole Premier League outing this season came in a 3-0 loss to Brentford, when he featured for 68 minutes before being taken off. He has since found himself excluded from the first-team picture.
