“Nigeria must become a nation where no citizen is punished for demanding good governance and a better future,” Obi said in a statement posted on X on Tuesday.

Obi described the anniversary as a reminder of the price Nigerian youths paid in their demand for a better country.

“Today, October 20, 2026, marks the sixth anniversary of the Lekki Toll Gate shootings, a painful reminder of the price Nigerian youths paid in their demand for a better country.”

He recalled the events of October 20, 2020, saying peaceful protesters faced gunfire and that lives were lost, and many people were injured, leaving questions about justice, accountability and the value placed on human life.

“On that fateful night, peaceful #EndSARS protesters were met with gunfire. Lives were lost, many were injured, and the nation was left with questions about justice, accountability, and the sanctity of human life.”

Calling on Nigerians to remember the victims and resist treating injustice as normal, Obi said: “We must never forget. We must never normalise injustice.”

He also noted that the anniversary reinforced his belief in a “New Nigeria,” describing it as a country where citizens are protected, young people are heard, and those in government exercise power responsibly and respect human rights.

“As we remember the victims, I reaffirm my belief that a New Nigeria is possible—a country where citizens are protected, not brutalised; where young people are heard, not silenced; and where government power is exercised with responsibility and respect for human rights.”

Obi added that the victims’ sacrifice should strengthen efforts to ensure the incident is not repeated while praying for those who died.

“May the souls of the departed continue to rest in peace. May their sacrifice strengthen our resolve to build a Nigeria where this tragedy will never be repeated.”

He ended the statement by reiterating his vision of a country where every life matters.

The Lagos State Judicial Panel of Inquiry’s 2021 report found that Nigerian Army officers shot, injured and killed unarmed protesters at the Lekki Toll Gate, and said the manner of assault and killing could be described as a massacre in context. Vanguard reported that the panel identified at least 48 protesters who were shot, injured or assaulted.

World.title: Police disrupt #EndSARS memorial at Lekki tollgate, tear gas Rhodes-Vivour, Doherty
World.content:
By Esther Onyegbula

Police officers on Tuesday fired tear gas to disperse residents, journalists, activists and political figures gathered at the Lekki tollgate in Lagos to commemorate victims of the October 2020 #EndSARS protests.

Among those affected by the police action were the Lagos State governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty.

The memorial, organised by the Enough is Enough movement, was aimed at honouring those who lost their lives during the #EndSARS protests and remembering the nationwide demonstrations against police brutality.

The gathering was, however, disrupted before participants could lay wreaths at the tollgate, as police officers deployed to the venue fired tear gas canisters to disperse the crowd.

The action triggered confusion as participants scrambled for safety amid clouds of tear gas that spread across the area.

Following the incident, participants fled the scene as the gas filled the vicinity, forcing the disruption of the planned commemoration.

The memorial was part of activities to remember the victims of the #EndSARS protests, which drew widespread public attention in October 2020 over allegations of police brutality, particularly against young Nigerians.

The Lekki tollgate became a focal point of the protests and has remained a significant site for subsequent commemorations by activists and other Nigerians demanding accountability, justice and reforms in the country’s policing system.

Tuesday’s incident prevented participants from completing the planned wreath-laying ceremony, which was intended to pay tribute to those who lost their lives during the protests.

Meanwhile, the Lagos State Police Command is yet to provide an explanation for the use of tear gas at the time of filing this report.

World.title: Uduaghan’s demise, shocking, great loss to Nigeria – Akpabio
World.content:
Uduaghan

Says his tenure as the state Governor marked a very significant moment in the infrastructural development of the state

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA- THE President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio has mourned the death of former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan who died just three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family.

Akpabio has said Uduaghan’s tenure as the state Governor marked a very significant moment in the infrastructural development of the state as he described his death as shocking, a great loss to Nigeria and the entire people of the Niger Delta region.

In a statement signed yesterday by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, Akpabio said, “I received with profound shock and disbelief the news of the transition of Dr Uduaghan at the age of 71, just three days to his 72nd birthday.

“Dr Uduaghan was the governor of Delta State from 2007- 2015, when I also had the opportunity to preside over the affairs of Akwa Ibom State as their governor. He was a distinguished medical doctor and a committed statesman, who devoted his life to public office.

” His tenure as the state Governor marked a very significant moment in the infrastructural development of the state. He was a committed leader to the healthcare delivery and human capital development of his people. He was a bridge-builder across the Niger Delta region and Nigeria as a whole. He was a detribalised leader and a respected elder whose contributions to democracy and national development will be sorely missed.

“On behalf of the 10th Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, I extend our deepest condolences to the larger Uduaghan family, his wife, Mrs Roli Uduaghan, the children, the people and Government of Delta State, and the Itsekiri nation and indeed the entire Niger Delta on the passing of their illustrous son and former Governor of Delta State.

“May Almighty God grant his gentle soul eternal rest and grant his family and the people of Delta State the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,”

World.title: Power outage hits Google Cloud services, disrupting UK banks
World.content:
A power outage at a Google Cloud data centre near London caused serious failures to services on Tuesday, the US technology giant said, as several UK banks reported widespread disruptions.

Google said in a service update that its Cloud services suffered an outage “due to a power event”, adding that a full recovery was expected at around 1300 GMT on Tuesday.

Services for the digital bank Revolut, including withdrawals from ATMs, bank transfers and bank card top-ups, were disrupted, which a source close to the matter attributed to the Google Cloud failures.

UK lenders Lloyds and HSBC also confirmed customers were facing issues with their banking services.

Google said the incident began at 0608 GMT on Tuesday.

“Multiple Google Cloud services are experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region,” Google said in an earlier update, referring to its London data centre.

Internet service tracker Downdetector indicated that hundreds of reports had been made of problems affecting other businesses, including the property website Rightmove and the Royal Mail postal service.

Lloyds said it was aware “some customers are having issues with our app and online banking”.

HSBC confirmed that customers were experiencing “difficulties accessing our services” and said that it would “monitor the situation, which is also affecting other organisations”.

A Revolut spokesperson said the bank was “working to fix the issue since it was identified” and offered its apologies “to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused”.

“We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe,” the spokesperson added in a statement.

AFP

World.title: Mourinho warns no ‘untouchable’ stars at Real Madrid
World.content:
Real Madrid’s Portuguese coach Jose Mourinho reacts during the UEFA Champions League – 1st round day 2 football match between AS Roma and Real Madrid at the Olympic Stadium in Rome on October 14, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP)

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho on Tuesday warned Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior and the team’s other stars that no-one is “untouchable”.

Vinicius has struggled for form this season and is serving a four-match ban in La Liga for hair-pulling, but is available as Madrid host RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, the club’s record 140 million euro ($157m) signing, has impressed in recent weeks, scoring against Sevilla on Sunday in La Liga in Vinicius’s absence.

“Only the club badge is untouchable,” Mourinho told reporters when asked if Vinicius’s place in the team was in danger given Diomande’s form.

“I don’t like the concept of untouchable players.

“What makes a player untouchable is not his status, the armband, his years at the club, how much was paid for him, what makes him untouchable is his performance on the pitch.”

Mourinho said Vinicius would play on the left wing against Leipzig and he had not yet told Diomande whether he would start as well.

Madrid host the Bundesliga side aiming for a third Champions League victory from three matches in the league phase, but in La Liga they are third and six points behind leaders Barcelona, who they visit on Sunday.

Mourinho said the team’s level is still a long way from where he hopes he can take it.

“A long way off… we’ve been here three or four months, it’s impossible to be where we want to be,” continued the veteran Portuguese coach.

“We always have to improve, be it individually or collectively… I understand the demands (at this club) are the maximum.

“I’ve been here three years (2010-2013), and so I know perfectly well how things are. I can’t lose my direction… (even though) I know there is a lot of work to do.”

French defender Ibrahima Konate said the former Chelsea and Manchester United coach commanded respect.

“He’s a great manager, I think he has this aura that not many managers have, because he doesn’t need to speak and everyone will listen and respect him,” Konate told reporters.

World.title: Cultism: Police arrest two suspects, recover locally made pistol in Ajah
World.content:
By Esther Onyegbula

Operatives of the Lagos State Police Command’s Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) have arrested two suspected cultists allegedly terrorising residents of Addo Road, Ajah, Lagos, and recovered a locally made cut-to-size pistol.

The suspects, identified as Idris Rasak, 26, aka Aloss, and Ibrahim Kazeem, 25, aka Asunmo Kebe, were arrested following intelligence reports about their alleged involvement in cult-related activities in the area.

The police said the suspects, during interrogation, reportedly confessed to being members of the Eiye Confraternity and subsequently led operatives to the Waterside area of Addo, Ajah, where the firearm was recovered.

The development is part of efforts by the Lagos State Police Command to curb cultism and other violent crimes through intelligence-led operations.

In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, Lagos State Command, SP Abimbola Adebisi, the command said the arrest followed credible intelligence on the alleged activities of the suspects.

According to the statement, the operatives acted on information concerning the suspects’ alleged involvement in cult-related activities within the Addo Road area of Ajah.

“During interrogation, the suspects reportedly confessed to being members of the Eiye Confraternity and led operatives to the Waterside area of Addo, Ajah, where a locally made cut-to-size pistol was recovered,” the statement said.

The police said the suspects were currently in custody, while investigations were ongoing to determine the full extent of their alleged activities and identify other persons who might be connected to the reported criminal acts.

The recovery of the firearm is expected to form part of the ongoing investigation as detectives work to establish the circumstances surrounding its possession and whether it was connected to any criminal activity.

Cult-related violence remains a security concern in parts of Lagos, with suspected clashes and other violent incidents capable of threatening residents’ safety and disrupting normal activities in affected communities.

The latest arrests underscore the importance of intelligence gathering and public cooperation in identifying suspected criminal activities and preventing violence.

The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command, CP Tijani Fatai, reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling cultism and other criminal activities across the state.

He urged members of the public to provide credible information to the police to support crime prevention and enhance the safety and security of residents.

The command said it would continue to deploy intelligence-led strategies to identify and apprehend persons suspected of involvement in criminal activities.

World.title: How Grassroots Innovation Challenge Became Part of Nigeria’s Industrial Policy
World.content:
Ayodeji Ake

At the State House, the Federal Government framed InnovateNaija as more than an awards night. It set the programme inside a larger argument about what Nigeria makes, and what it should stop importing.

The message President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sent to the InnovateNaija ceremony on October 7 was less about prizes than about production. Delivered by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, it described the awards as an investment in the innovators’ ability to contribute to Nigeria’s economic and industrial transformation. The president’s agenda, the minister said, puts a productive, inclusive and resilient economy at the centre, measured in decent jobs, stronger local industries, more exports and better livelihoods. Science, technology, and innovation sit at the heart of that plan.

Udeh restated the government’s commitment to “home-grown technological solutions towards Nigeria’s industrialization”, and stressed that research, investment and industry must work together to turn the country’s people and natural resources into productive capacity.

Quality, Not Patriotism

One line from the minister deserves more attention than it received. He said Nigerian-made products should win buyers because they meet the required standard and offer value, not only because they are Nigerian. That is a demanding test. It asks local manufacturers to compete head-on with imports, and it asks the government to back them with the testing, certification, and infrastructure that make quality possible.

NASENI’s Executive Vice-Chairman, Khalil Suleiman Halilu, set out how the agency intends to meet that test. In a keynote titled ‘Nigeria’s Innovation Era,’ he said the country must move decisively from consumption to creation. NASENI is reorganising its research and development work around three principles: Creation, Collaboration and Commercialisation. In his telling, Nigeria does not lack ideas or talent; it lacks strong links to prototypes and production, and between innovators and industry.

The Machinery Behind the Mandate

NASENI has physical assets to put behind that ambition. When the challenge was launched in 2025, the agency said winners would join its innovation hub incubation programme and gain access to its 12 institutes and centre of excellence in Abuja, with their machinery, laboratories and manufacturing support. The launch carried a slogan that sums up the policy: with the right support, “Nigerian ingenuity becomes Nigerian industry.”

The finalists show why that support matters. Zang Luka of Plateau State makes USB cables in Nigeria but still imports about 60 per cent of his materials, and he has asked government for help with machinery, tools and production space so he can scale up and eventually export across Africa. His case illustrates the distance between making a product locally and building a local supply chain.

States Join the Effort

Industrialisation is not only a federal project. The governors of Abia, Anambra, Enugu, Plateau and Kaduna matched NASENI’s N2.5 million state grants. Kaduna’s Deputy Governor, Dr Hadiza Sabuwa Balarabe, called InnovateNaija “a renaissance of Nigerian ingenuity” and argued that a modern nation’s wealth is measured as much by its people’s inventiveness as by its natural resources. Her state’s own champion, Abdulrahaman Bin Umar of Anchau, built a drone that can spray up to 11 hectares of farmland in an hour.

What Will Prove the Mandate

Policy statements are cheap; factories are not. The test of this industrialisation push will be visible in a few concrete places: whether the National Research and Innovation Development Fund bill becomes law and is funded, whether NASENI’s institutes actually produce for the winners at scale, and whether products like PenKeep and the Smart Pond reach buyers at a price that beats the imported alternative.

InnovateNaija has shown that the inventors exist in every state. The industrial policy built around them now has to show it can carry their products from the workshop to the market.

World.title: LACCOSA Alumni Celebrate 50 Years, Reaffirms Commitment to Education
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

As the 1976 set of the Lagos City College Old Students’ Association (LACCOSA) marks its 50 years since graduating from the institution, it has reaffirmed its commitment to educational development through infrastructure provision, scholarships, laboratory rehabilitation and student mentorship.

Speaking at a press conference, Monday to herald the anniversary celebrations themed, ‘Uncommon Grace’, the Chairman of the anniversary committee, Dave Nwanze, explained that the association had consistently supported its alma mater, through projects and initiatives aimed at improving teaching and learning.

He emphasised its interventions in the provision of student desks and lockers, water facilities, solar power, learning equipment and scholarships, adding that it has also sustained a scholarship programme for 40 students sponsored by its North American members over the past three to four years.

“The association has also rehabilitated the school’s Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Agricultural Science laboratories, while providing photocopiers, laptops and other essential facilities to support academic activities,” he said.

The initiative, the chairman noted, has helped beneficiaries improve their academic performance, with some using their results to secure admission into universities.

Beyond infrastructure and financial assistance, Nwanze said the association has also organised career talks, mentorship programmes and other activities designed to inspire students and prepare them for future opportunities.

As part of this year’s golden jubilee celebrations, he said it plans to further recognise outstanding students in the sciences, commercial subjects and arts, with awards intended to encourage academic excellence and motivate other learners.

The celebrations, scheduled to hold from October 19 to 24, will feature activities designed to reconnect members with their alma mater and strengthen the association’s contribution to education.

On October 21, members will return to Lagos City College for mentorship lectures on the theme, ‘Path to Success’, the inauguration of a corporate social responsibility project and an interreligious thanksgiving service.

The celebrations, Nwanze said, will culminate in a grand finale gala night on October 24, at the Radisson Blu Hotel, GRA, Ikeja, Lagos.

The chairman emphasised that the anniversary theme reflects its gratitude to God for sustaining members over the past five decades and providing an opportunity to give back to the institution that shaped their formative years.

The anniversary also comes as the school prepares to expand its academic offerings.

According to him, approval for the establishment of a junior secondary school section was secured recently, marking a significant development in the institution’s history.

The development, he stated, is expected to provide a pathway for younger pupils to progress from junior to senior secondary education within the school.

On his assesment of the education sector over the years, an alumnus of the college, Kunle Sanyaolu, said the increasing number of students, without a corresponding expansion of infrastructure and teaching resources, could limit interactions between teachers and learners and affect students’ acquisition of knowledge.

He stated that the learning environment had changed considerably since the alumni graduated from the institution five decades ago.

Sanyaolu recalled that: “Students in our time had more opportunities to interact with teachers because of the relatively manageable number of learners in their classrooms.”

He, however, expressed concern that the increasing student population could make such interactions more difficult, particularly where the number of teachers and available facilities had not kept pace with enrolment.

He said: “When you have one teacher to so many students, that means the teacher-student ratio becomes a concern. That is something we did not quite experience in our time because we had the opportunity to interact with our teachers.”

Sanyaolu also emphasised the pressure on school infrastructure, citing the assembly hall, which served students when the alumni were in school.

According to him, the facilities available five decades ago may no longer be sufficient to accommodate the current student population, potentially creating congestion and affecting the overall learning experience.

He said these challenges, directly or indirectly, could influence the quality of education and knowledge acquired by students.

Sanyaolu urged stakeholders to pay greater attention to the relationship between student enrolment, teacher availability and school infrastructure in efforts to improve educational outcomes.

World.title: DSS Arraigns Five Suspected Kidnappers of 20 Youth Corps Members, Others
World.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) on Tuesday arraigned five men before the Imo State High Court over the alleged kidnapping of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and four other persons in the state.

Three of the defendants, Usman Aliyu, 25, also known as Chonge; Babangida Aliyu, 21; and Mohammed Ali, 23, aka Smallie Pepper, were arraigned over the abduction of the prospective corps members on Independence Day.

The remaining two defendants, Aminu Haliru, 27, and Tange Ibrahim, 20, aka Jijji, were accused of kidnapping four persons on October 4.

The five defendants face charges bordering on conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms.

According to the prosecution, the three defendants in the first case, alongside other suspects still at large, allegedly abducted the prospective corps members along the Owerri–Mgbidi–Onitsha Expressway on October 1.

The victims were reportedly travelling from Ibadan to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states when they were kidnapped. They were rescued after seven days.

The defendants were charged with conspiracy to commit hostage-taking, punishable under Section 6 of the Imo State Prohibition of Hostage Taking and Related Offences Law No. 4 of 2009.

According to the charge sheet filed at the Imo State High Court, Oru Judicial Division, Mgbidi, the defendants were also accused of unlawfully possessing three AK-47 rifles, four magazines, a pistol and 81 rounds of live ammunition.

In the second case, prosecutors alleged that Haliru, Ibrahim and others still at large kidnapped four persons around Owerri and Mgbidi on October 4.

The prosecution further alleged that the defendants collected N8 million as ransom for the release of the victims.

They also face charges of unlawfully possessing one AK-47 rifle and a pump-action gun.

The prosecution listed N1.8 million as money recovered in the second case.

A DSS investigator and the victims were listed as witnesses in both cases.

World.title: ECOWAS Court Judges Vow to End Delays, Enforce Judgments
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The newly appointed judges of the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice have pledged to uphold judicial independence and integrity, tackle delays in adjudication and strengthen compliance with the court’s judgments, amid renewed emphasis on restoring public confidence in regional justice delivery.

The judges made the commitment as they began a five-day orientation programme on Monday, against the backdrop of growing institutional demands for timely justice, impartial adjudication and effective enforcement of judicial decisions across the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

President of the Court, Justice Charlyne Brumskine, who outlined the priorities of the new judicial college, said the credibility of the regional court depended on the fairness, impartiality and integrity demonstrated in every case.

Brumskine, in her opening address, challenged the judges to make judicial excellence, collegiality and effective adjudication the defining principles of their tenure, stressing that their responsibilities extended beyond the determination of disputes to strengthening confidence in the court as a regional judicial institution.

She identified judicial independence and integrity, collegiality, and effectiveness as the three priorities that must guide the new college, emphasising the need for rigorous deliberations, mutual respect and consistency in judicial decisions.

The court president also highlighted the need to address delays in the administration of justice, insisting on the importance of timely adjudication and alignment with the court’s Strategic Plan for 2026–2030.

A major concern she raised was compliance with the court’s judgments, calling for sustained engagement with ECOWAS member states to strengthen implementation of its decisions.

The emphasis on compliance places the relationship between the court and member states at the centre of efforts to improve the effectiveness of regional justice, as the authority of a court depends not only on the judgments it delivers but also on their implementation.

Congratulating the judges on their assumption of office on October 13, Brumskine said service at the regional court required a thorough understanding of the ECOWAS legal order, the court’s jurisdiction and procedures, and its jurisprudence developed over more than two decades.

The five-day orientation, themed ‘Becoming an ECOWAS Judge: Judicial Excellence, Institutional Integration and Effective Adjudication,’ is intended to prepare the judges for the demands of their judicial responsibilities and familiarise them with the institution’s operational framework.

In his welcome address, the Acting Chief Registrar, Dr Ousmane Diallo, said the programme was designed to ensure the smooth integration of the judges and their executive assistants into the court’s institutional and administrative systems.

He said participants would be introduced to the court’s organisational structure, departmental responsibilities, administrative procedures and coordination mechanisms, while gaining a clearer understanding of the roles of judicial, legal, administrative and other support services.

Diallo added that the programme would strengthen communication and collaboration among judges, executive assistants, heads of departments and other staff, with the ultimate objective of improving institutional continuity and operational efficiency.

The expected outcomes include a better understanding of the court’s support systems, stronger professional relationships and improved staff preparedness to assist the new judicial college in discharging its functions.

Other judges participating in the orientation are Justice Désire Henri Aihou, Vice-President of the Court; Justice Henrietta Uzoamaka Didigu; Justice Yaouza Ouro-Sama; and Justice Awa Bah.

Brumskine acknowledged the contributions of Diallo, the facilitator and former vice-president of the court, Professor Friday C. Nwoke, and the court’s staff to the organisation of the programme.

The orientation marks the beginning of the new judges’ integration into the court’s institutional framework, with judicial independence, integrity, timely justice and compliance with judgments identified as central to strengthening the delivery of justice within the West African regional community.

World.title: Saudi Arabia Aid Group Carries Out Cardiac Surgery on Indegent Patients in Abuja
World.content:
*Targets 108 procedures

Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has conducted voluntary medical outreach in Nigeria to provide specialised cardiac treatment, targeting 108 procedures including 28 open-heart surgeries and 80 diagnostic and therapeutic cardiac catheterisation.

The initiative is being implemented under the auspices King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) in collaboration with Al-Balsam Association for Health Training and Development.

The campaign is designed to help patients access advanced cardiac care, particularly those whose financial circumstances limit their treatment options.

During first four days of campaign, medical team i performed 75 procedures, comprising 10 open-heart surgeries and 65 interventional cardiac catheterisation procedures.

The team also conducted 13 medical examinations and provided consultations and other essential medical services.

The procedures are being carried out at Nizamiye and Zenith Hospitals in Abuja, where 10 Saudi volunteers, including specialist doctors, consultants, nurses, technicians and administrative personnel, are working alongside Nigerian medical professionals to assess patients and deliver treatment in clinical settings and operating rooms.

Yousef bin Mohammed Al-Balawi, Ambassador of Custodian of Two Holy Mosques to Federal Republic of Nigeria, visited Al-Balsam medical team at Zenith Hospital in Abuja to observe campaign’s activities.

The envoy expressed satisfaction with organisation and level of care provided and commended cooperation between Saudi volunteers and Nigerian health workers.

The campaign forms part of KSrelief’s international voluntary medical programme, which deploys specialist teams to countries in need to provide treatment and support healthcare delivery in communities where access to advanced medical services may be limited.

Through initiative, Saudi Arabia is extending its medical assistance to Nigerian patients requiring specialised cardiac interventions while promoting cooperation between Saudi and Nigerian healthcare professionals.

Officials said initiative will ease burden on patients who cannot afford expensive cardiac surgeries abroad and will also facilitate knowledge sharing between two countries.

The programme adds to Kingdom’s wider international assistance efforts, with specialised medical missions providing practical support to patients and families facing barriers to essential treatment.

Stakeholders said intervention is timely given rising cases of cardiovascular diseases in Nigeria and limited facilities for open-heart surgeries in public hospitals.

The ongoing campaign is expected to run for several days, with beneficiaries drawn from Abuja and other parts of country after screening and evaluation.

World.title: United Nigeria Airlines Delivers Community Health Centre to Ekiti, As Oyebanji Pledges Equipment, Medical Personnel
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

United Nigeria Airlines has reinforced the growing role of Nigeria’s private sector in supporting public infrastructure with the construction and handover of a modern community health centre, a solar-powered borehole and perimeter fence to the Ekiti State Government, describing the intervention as a demonstration of the power of public-private partnership in accelerating grassroots development.

The facilities, located at Aso-Ayegunle in Ado-Ekiti, were inaugurated by Ekiti State Governor, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, who pledged that the state government would immediately equip the health centre, deploy qualified medical personnel and integrate it into the state’s primary healthcare system to provide quality healthcare services for residents.

Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, said the intervention reflected the airline’s commitment to ensuring that communities where it operates benefited directly from its presence, stressing that businesses must contribute meaningfully to national development beyond their commercial activities.

He said the project underscored the importance of public-private partnerships in bridging infrastructure gaps, particularly in critical sectors such as healthcare where government resources alone might not be sufficient to meet growing demands.

Okonkwo commended Governor Oyebanji for creating an enabling environment for private investment, describing the governor’s collaborative approach as a major factor that inspired the airline’s decision to undertake the project.

According to him, the Ekiti State Government selected United Nigeria Airlines as its preferred carrier after carrying out due diligence on the company’s operations and capacity, adding that the airline considered it appropriate to reciprocate the confidence by investing directly in the welfare of the host community.

He explained that rather than merely operating flights into the state, the airline chose to leave a lasting developmental legacy capable of improving the quality of life of residents.

Okonkwo disclosed that United Nigeria Airlines had implemented similar corporate social responsibility interventions across the country, including humanitarian support for flood-ravaged communities in Bayelsa State and development projects in Anambra State, adding that more interventions were planned nationwide.

Describing the Ekiti project as unique, he said it symbolised the success of strategic collaboration between government and the private sector and demonstrated how such partnerships could deliver tangible benefits to local communities.

He also reaffirmed the airline’s commitment to supporting Ekiti’s tourism and agricultural development, expressing readiness to partner with the state in the transportation of agricultural produce as export opportunities expand.

Governor Oyebanji, in his remarks, expressed appreciation to the airline for complementing his administration’s efforts to expand access to quality primary healthcare across the state.

The governor explained that the understanding reached with the airline was for the company to construct the facility while the state government would provide the necessary equipment, deploy healthcare workers and ensure its effective operation.

He assured residents that the Ministry of Health would immediately commence the process of integrating the facility into the state’s primary healthcare network to guarantee efficient service delivery.

Oyebanji urged members of the community to take ownership of the facility by protecting and maintaining it, noting that it would significantly reduce the burden of travelling long distances to access healthcare, especially for pregnant women, nursing mothers and children.

Also speaking, the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe, described the project as a landmark development for Aso-Ayegunle and commended both the airline and the state government for bringing meaningful development to the community.

The monarch recalled the initial opposition to the acquisition of land for the Ekiti Agro-Allied International Cargo Airport but noted that the benefits of the project were now becoming evident through investments such as the new health centre.

Speaking on behalf of residents, Mr. Fajuyi Olumide expressed appreciation to United Nigeria Airlines and the Ekiti State Government for the intervention, saying the project had renewed hope among members of the community and would greatly improve access to healthcare.

He expressed optimism that the initiative would open the door for additional development projects capable of transforming the socio-economic well-being of the area.

World.title: Group Tasks Youths on Character Moulding, Decision Making
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

A group, Fasttrack Development Initiative (FDI) has called on youths to build right character and take decisive actions to achieve a better future.

Executive Director of FDI, Mr Justus Ngerebara gave the charge at their Annual Emerging Leaders Conference with the theme “Choices, Character and the Future,” held in Port Harcourt at the weekend.

Represented by his Executive Secretary, Dr. Ineme-Awaji John, the FDI Executive Director emphasised that youths in the present life are gradually loosing focus necessitating the need for proper guidance and coaching.

He noted that character and choices a young person makes can either make or mar their future, adding that the conference was to re engineer their thought processes and help them realign their mindsets towards achieving their life goals.

“Our vision is actually to re-engineer the minds of the youth, their thought process, and to force them to achieve greater future endeavor in their life. We have come to see and understand that in this society of today, many youths have lost focus, many youths no longer believe in themselves, many youths don’t think that there is a future for themselves. You could have seen and heard from many of them who would say, adulthood is a scam.

“So we are preparing them to believe that adulthood indeed is not a scambut there is a place in the future for them, not just today, but our tomorrow is greater. So we are creating a scenario and an avenue for them to move forward in rebranding their thought process, rebranding their expectations in life. That’s why we think that character is a key thing to begin with, ” he stated.

Speaking on the year’s theme, he noted, “Changing your character and having a better attitude for tomorrow will revisit your choices that you make in life, and ultimately create a better future for you tomorrow.”

The FDI director charged youths to dream big, believe in themselves and pursue their dreams legitimately while assuring them of a greater future ahead.

Delivering a lecture on making right choices, a chartered conciliator and former National Deputy President of the Institute of Chartered Mediators and Conciliators, Dr. Ken-Fashola Ayibaemi, stated that choices have consequences, charging participsnts that whatever choices they make have consequences that can meet them at irreversible points.

Ayibaemi stated that the future is shaped by choices, pointing out that the quality of ones future is as result of present day choices.

The guest lecturer warned youths not to be lured by immediate benefits to make damaging choices.

“What is right is right, what is wrong is wrong, inspite of the immediate benefitswhat is right is right, what is wrong is wrong, ” he stated.

While commending FDI for helping to shape the choices of youths in the country, Ayibaemi called on other organisations and government in particular to provide the right leadership atmosphere for youths to develop and bring their dreams to reality.

“Government should take responsibility, government is a creator,government should take responsibility for its duties, create environments, empower people, create atmospheres, create opportunities, even if it’s not directly to the youths.

Look at where we are today, look at the opportunities that is being created by an individual, if government enables people, good people will arise, responsible people will arise and they will encourage youths, and that is where we are today,” he stressed.

Our correspondent reports that the event attracted over 600 youths cutting across the entire country in attendance, also had Emeka Nobis and Pastor Jackson Adebisi as speakers.

World.title: Why Gov Otu Deserves Second Term, By Obono-Obla
World.content:
A former presidential aide and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Okoi Obono-Obla is confident that Governor Bassey Otu of Cross River State will win his second term election by a landslide.

Obono-Obla who was speaking on Arise News programme NewsNight, hinged his confidence on what he described as the Governor’s performance and management of the state’s finances.

While stating that opposition in the state has been weakened by internal strife, he said Otu inherited a state facing significant financial challenges, including substantial debt and difficulties paying workers’ salaries.

According to him, Otu has managed to address these challenges creditably well without resort to borrowing.

He also highlighted an increase in the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), stating that it rose from approximately ₦21 billion in 2022 to nearly ₦76 billion in 2026.

Obono-Obla maintained that Governor Otu’s handling of the state’s financial challenges, efforts to improve internally generated revenue, and overall performance makes his re-election a foregone conclusion.

On efforts by opposition parties to present a single presidential candidate against President Bola Tinubu, he dismissed the idea as a mere comic relief.

World.title: New labour laws could change the rules for domestic workers in South Africa
World.content:
South African households employing undocumented foreign domestic workers could face hefty fines under proposed amendments to employment legislation. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South African households employing undocumented foreign domestic workers could face hefty fines under proposed amendments to employment legislation, while still being legally required to honour workers’ wage and employment claims.

The proposed Employment Services Amendment Bill, tabled in Parliament, seeks to strengthen enforcement against the unlawful employment of foreign nationals and introduce penalties for employers who breach immigration and labour laws.

The proposed changes could have significant implications for private households that employ foreign domestic workers, particularly those who believe a worker’s immigration status means they can pay below the legal minimum wage or disregard other employment obligations.



Penalties

Under the proposed framework, employers could face a R100 000 fine for a first offence, with penalties potentially increasing to R1 million or resulting in imprisonment for further violations.

The Bill remains under consideration, and its proposed provisions should not be confused with legislation already in force.

Domestic workers could still claim minimum wage

Section 12D of the proposed Bill provides that workers unlawfully employed in South Africa would retain the right to pursue employment-related claims against their employers.

These could include claims involving unpaid wages, minimum-wage violations and other breaches of applicable labour legislation or collective agreements.

The Department of Employment and Labour said the provision “seeks to prevent unscrupulous employers from employing foreign nationals on terms and conditions of employment that are inferior to those provided for by labour legislation and collective agreements”.

Labour inspectors and bargaining council agents could also pursue claims on behalf of workers who are unable to enforce their rights themselves.



The proposed amendments aim to close loopholes that allow employers to avoid their obligations by exploiting a worker’s undocumented status.

These obligations can include paying the prescribed minimum wage and meeting applicable registration requirements for the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Compensation Fund.

The proposed penalties for unlawful employment would apply to employers across the country, including private households.

Minimum wage stands at R30.23 an hour

The developments come as South Africa’s national minimum wage stands at R30.23 an hour, effective from 1 March 2026.

The rate increased from R28.79 an hour and applies to domestic workers, farm workers and other employees covered by the national minimum wage provisions.

For a domestic worker completing a typical 160-hour working month, the minimum-wage equivalent is approximately R4 837 before deductions.

However, actual monthly earnings depend on the hours worked, and employers must comply with the applicable rules governing working hours, overtime and other employment conditions.

Compliance remains a concern in the domestic-work sector.

Statistics South Africa data cited in reporting on domestic-worker pay put the median monthly salary at R2 350 – substantially below the minimum-wage equivalent for a 160-hour month.

The gap highlights the challenges facing workers whose wages fall below the legal minimum, as well as the potential consequences for employers who fail to comply.

What employers need to know

The proposed amendments reinforce the distinction between immigration compliance and employment rights.

Employers may be prohibited from employing foreign nationals who do not have the required authorisation to work in South Africa. However, that does not automatically remove the worker’s ability to pursue employment-related claims.

In practical terms, employers cannot assume that hiring an undocumented foreign national allows them to avoid paying wages owed or complying with applicable labour protections.

The Bill also seeks to establish a legislative framework for labour migration and introduce sector-specific quotas for the employment of foreign nationals.

The Employment Services Amendment Bill was approved by Cabinet for introduction to Parliament before being referred to the Portfolio Committee on Employment and Labour for consideration.

The public-comment period runs until 6 November 2026, giving interested parties an opportunity to submit their views on the proposed changes.

Written submissions should be addressed to the Portfolio Committee on Employment and Labour, for the attention of Mr Zolani Sakasa, at employmentservicesbill@parliament.gov.za.

World.title: The best places to see lions in Kruger National Park
World.content:
From Satara to the southern plains, here are the Kruger areas worth trying for lion sightings. Image: canva

Seeing a lion in the wild is high on the list for many visitors to the Kruger National Park.

Lions occur throughout Kruger, so there is no guaranteed road or camp where you will find them.

However, some areas have reputations for particularly good lion sightings. Take a look.



Where to see lions in Kruger

Area Why visit Good base Satara Open habitat and strong big-cat sightings Satara Lower Sabie High diversity of predators and prey Lower Sabie Crocodile Bridge Known for numerous lion prides Crocodile Bridge Orpen–Satara Open plains and plentiful grazing animals Orpen or Satara Olifants area Lion regularly recorded alongside other big game Olifants Northern Kruger Quieter and less crowded Punda Maria

Satara is one of the top choices

If lions are the main reason for your trip, Satara is an obvious place to start.

SANParks describes the area as one of the best game-viewing regions in Kruger and says it is particularly noted for big cats, with lion, leopard and cheetah regularly recorded.

The relatively open vegetation also makes it easier to scan the landscape compared with some of the thicker areas of the park.

Don’t overlook Lower Sabie

Lower Sabie is another strong option. The area around the Sabie River supports large numbers of prey species, while SANParks specifically lists lion among the animals regularly found in the area.

The combination of riverine areas, open sections and productive roads makes the southern part of Kruger a good all-round predator-viewing destination.

Try the Crocodile Bridge area

Crocodile Bridge is another area worth considering if lions are a priority.



SANParks describes the surrounding southern section, known as the Southern Circle, as being renowned for its concentration of different lion prides.

The area also has plenty of general game, which means there is a good prey base for predators.

Look early and late

Timing also matters. Lions are often more active during the cooler parts of the day, particularly early morning and later afternoon. This is also when temperatures are more comfortable for many other animals.

If you’re self-driving, getting out early gives you more time on the road before the day heats up.

Don’t rush past a stationary lion, either. A pride may spend much of the day resting before becoming active again later.

It’s also important to remember that even in areas famous for lions, sightings are never guaranteed. Kruger National Park’s wildlife is free-ranging, and conditions change constantly. A road that produced several lion sightings one day can be quiet the next.

That is part of what makes a self-drive safari exciting. If lions are particularly important to you, consider staying several nights in one of the better-known big-cat areas rather than trying to cover the entire park.

World.title: Two East London beaches closed after fatal shark attack
World.content:
Orient Beach and Eastern Beach in East London have been closed until further notice following a shark attack at Orient Beach on Tuesday. Image: Beaches Searcher

Orient Beach and Eastern Beach in East London have been closed until further notice following a shark attack at Orient Beach around 08:00 on Tuesday.

Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality issued a public safety warning, confirming that the incident had resulted in the tragic death of a woman.

The woman has been identified as 65-year-old Janine Lochrenberg, a retired nuclear radiographer and musician.



WATCH | Great white shark spotted in False Bay for first time in eight years

Authorities are currently at the scene dealing with the incident, while members of the public have been urged to stay away from the affected beaches.

The municipality has warned beachgoers not to enter the water at either Orient Beach or Eastern Beach until further notice.



Other beaches also under warning

Safety warnings have also been issued for other beaches, with the public urged to remain vigilant and follow instructions from the relevant authorities.

Beachgoers are advised to comply with all safety notices and avoid taking unnecessary risks while the situation is being managed.

The municipality said further updates would be communicated as more information becomes available.



The circumstances surrounding the reported shark attack, including the identity of the victim and any further details about the incident, have not yet been provided in the notice.

This developing news story is being updated and more details will be published shortly. Please refresh the page for the fullest version.

World.title: Steve Komphela allegedly racially abused in Angola incident
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns assistant coach Steve Komphela has allegedly been subjected to racial abuse by Wiliete SC head coach Beto Bianchi before reportedly becoming involved in a physical altercation.

The alleged incident took place on Sunday after Sundowns played to a goalless draw against Wiliete in Angola in the CAF Champions League preliminary round.

Some reports have claimed that Komphela punched Bianchi, who was reportedly taken to hospital. Neither club nor CAF, however, has officially confirmed the circumstances surrounding the alleged incident.



Speaking on Metro FM, Andile Ncube claimed that Komphela was escorted out of the Tundavala National Stadium by police following an altercation involving members of the technical benches.

“Coach Steve Komphela left the stadium with cops in Angola. Steve Komphela can speak Portuguese; he understands it. He is very good with languages; he’s got a good grasp of Portuguese,” Ncube said.

“He was escorted out of the stadium because there was some form of altercation, from what I hear, with the bench. There were racial slurs, spitting. The coach spat on Coach Steve, and I know Coach Steve personally. I call him big brother,” he added.

Ncube suggested that Komphela may have been pushed to the limit, leading to a reaction that was out of character for the Sundowns assistant coach.

Steve Komphela gets ‘physical’

Meanwhile, Wiliete vice-president Vitorins Lunga Vicele addressed the alleged incident, indicating that the club intended to pursue the matter through the appropriate channels.

“It is something that should not happen, especially when we are talking about two professional teams. We will therefore lodge complaints with the relevant CAF bodies and the Angolan justice system,” he told Angolan publication Angop.



The incident remains unconfirmed by the clubs and CAF, with further details expected to emerge as the matter develops. Steve Komphela is surely going to be the talking point when the two teams clash again this weekend in the second leg.

World.title: These are South Africa’s best and worst Home Affairs offices
World.content:
Which are the best and worst Home Affairs offices in South Africa? Image: file

A new analysis of Google reviews has revealed South Africa’s best and worst-rated Home Affairs offices, with four KwaZulu-Natal offices featuring among the 10 lowest-rated in the country.

The Home Affairs office in eMakhazeni, Mpumalanga, came out on top, with an average rating of 4.56 stars from 147 reviews.

At the other end of the table, the Secunda Home Affairs office had the lowest rating, averaging just 1.90 stars from 148 reviews.



The figures come from SEO experts at SEO Backlinks, who analysed Google Maps listings for Home Affairs offices across South Africa.

The Western Cape performed particularly well, with four offices in the national top 10. These were Bredasdorp, Grabouw, Epping and Ceres.

KwaZulu-Natal also had one office in the top 10, with Ndwedwe recording an impressive 4.09-star average.

The 10 worst Home Affairs offices

Rank Home Affairs office Province Rating Reviews 1 Secunda Mpumalanga 1.90 148 2 Alberton Gauteng 1.95 534 3 Pietermaritzburg KwaZulu-Natal 1.95 258 4 Humansdorp Eastern Cape 1.95 131 5 Sasolburg Free State 1.99 112 6 Pinetown KwaZulu-Natal 2.00 273 7 Pavilion, Westville KwaZulu-Natal 2.01 181 8 Prospecton KwaZulu-Natal 2.08 244 9 Vredenburg Western Cape 2.08 143 10 Middelburg Mpumalanga 2.14 154

KwaZulu-Natal’s poor performance stood out in the study. The province had four offices in the national bottom 10: Pietermaritzburg, Pinetown, Pavilion in Westville and Prospecton.

The province’s performance becomes even more noticeable when the offices are considered as a group. Among the three provinces with at least 10 offices included in the ranking, KwaZulu-Natal had the lowest average rating.

Province Offices ranked Average rating Gauteng 30 3.01 Western Cape 23 3.01 KwaZulu-Natal 14 2.71

The national average across all 82 ranked offices was 2.90 stars. Gauteng and the Western Cape both averaged 3.01 stars, while KZN came in at 2.71.



How the ranking was calculated

The analysis used the DataForSEO Business Listings database to pull Google Maps listings for Department of Home Affairs offices across South Africa on 5 October 2026.

The researchers initially identified 442 listings.

Closed offices, duplicate listings and businesses that were not Home Affairs offices were excluded. Home Affairs desks operating inside bank branches were retained.

The final ranking included 82 offices with at least 100 Google reviews, covering 26 477 reviews in total.

Rather than simply using the rounded rating displayed by Google, the researchers calculated each office’s exact average using its one-, two-, three-, four- and five-star review counts.

Where offices had exactly the same average, the one with the larger proportion of one-star reviews was ranked lower.

The rankings reflect Google reviewer sentiment and do not necessarily represent official service-performance data from the Department of Home Affairs.

World.title: Pirates, Chiefs and Sundowns ALL in action on the SAME night
World.content:
South African football fans are in for a blockbuster night of cup action on Tuesday, 27 October, in the Carling Knockout Cup Round of 16. Image: X @OfficialPSL

South African football fans are in for a blockbuster night of cup action when Mamelodi Sundowns, Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs all take to the field on Tuesday, 27 October, in the Carling Knockout Cup Round of 16.

The three Betway Premiership giants will be in action simultaneously, with all three matches scheduled to kick off at 19:00.

Mamelodi Sundowns will host Marumo Gallants at Loftus Versfeld, Orlando Pirates will welcome Milford FC to Orlando Amstel Arena, while Kaizer Chiefs face TS Galaxy at FNB Stadium.



With a place in the quarter-finals at stake, the evening promises plenty of intrigue as the three clubs look to keep their cup ambitions alive.

Mamelodi Sundowns face Marumo Gallants test

Mamelodi Sundowns will have home advantage when they take on Gallants in Pretoria.

The Brazilians will be eager to progress in a competition that offers another opportunity to add silverware to their collection.

However, Marumo Gallants, last season’s beaten finalists, will be determined to upset the odds and book their place in the next round.

Orlando Pirates begin title defence

Defending champions Orlando Pirates will also be in action on Tuesday night when they face Milford FC at Orlando Amstel Arena.

The Buccaneers won last season’s Carling Knockout Cup after beating Marumo Gallants 1-0 in the final. They will now be looking to take another step towards retaining the trophy.



Milford, meanwhile, will have the chance to make a statement against one of South Africa’s biggest clubs.

Kaizer Chiefs face TS Galaxy

Kaizer Chiefs complete the trio of headline fixtures when they host TS Galaxy at FNB Stadium.

The Soweto giants will be hoping to progress in the knockout competition, but TS Galaxy will provide a challenging test as both teams target a place in the quarter-finals.

Carling Knockout Round of 16 fixtures

The Round of 16 begins on Saturday, 24 October, with Golden Arrows taking on Chippa United at King Zwelithini Stadium at 15:00. Polokwane City will then face Siwelele FC at Old Peter Mokaba Stadium at 18:00.

Sunday’s fixtures see Kruger United meet AmaZulu FC at Mbombela Stadium at 15:00, followed by Sekhukhune United against Richards Bay FC at New Peter Mokaba Stadium at 18:00.

Durban City will host Stellenbosch FC at Chatsworth Stadium on Wednesday, 28 October, at 19:00.

All Round of 16 matches will be decided over 90 minutes. If a match is all-square at full-time, extra time will be played, followed by a penalty shootout if necessary.

With three of the country’s biggest clubs all in action on the same night, Tuesday promises to be one of the standout dates on the Carling Knockout Cup calendar.

Mark it down now!

World.title: ‘Truly speaking, I’m not proud’: Young man’s frustration with SASSA boils over
World.content:
Koketso Mphaphathe, a man from Gauteng, has a blunt message for the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA). He wants the agency to step up for young people who, he says, are running out of options.

Mphaphathe holds a matric certificate and has experience in admin and office work. Yet he remains unemployed and is actively looking for work. He shared his story through The South African’s SASSA grant survey.

Declined application leaves job seeker struggling

Mphaphathe told The South African that he has had a declined or lapsed SASSA application. His biggest financial concern, he said, is unemployment.



Mphaphathe rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as very poor. When asked what one thing he would change about the agency, he pointed straight at its app and website, saying both need fixing.

He also said he has never applied for additional government support because he did not know what else was available to him.

Young job seeker willing to go wherever the work is

His frustration comes through clearly in his message to SASSA. He urged the agency to “do its work in office and help South African youth as we are suffering”.



“Truly speaking I’m not proud to be living in South Africa at this moment,” he added.

His story mirrors that of many young South Africans who hold qualifications but cannot find work, leaving families to stretch limited household income as far as it will go.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.



Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Tshwane resumes chlorination, but Bronkhorstspruit water remains unsafe
World.content:
PRETORIA - The City of Tshwane has resumed chlorinating the water supply in Bronkhorstspruit, but residents are still being warned not to use the water for drinking, cleaning or washing.

The Water and Sanitation Department says the chlorine problem has been resolved and new water entering the system is being treated.

However, untreated water may still be sitting in reservoirs and pipes, meaning the system needs to be thoroughly flushed before the water can be considered safe.

Residents are also being urged to clean containers previously used to store the potentially contaminated water, using a common household detergent before reusing them.

But a water infrastructure expert warns that the consequences of failing to disinfect the water could be far more serious.

World.title: Political assassinations may be driven by more than politics, researcher says
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Political killings tend to increase around local government elections, with competition for political power potentially linked to organised crime. That is the view of organised crime researcher Julian Rademeyer.

At least 43 people have been killed in suspected politically motivated attacks in the first nine months of this year.

Rademeyer says the violence is often more pronounced during local government election periods than during national elections.

READ | ANC condemns killing of two members during KZN campaign

“These kinds of killings intensify particularly around local government periods. You know, national elections, we still see some assassinations, but not nearly on this kind of level,” he says.

He believes the intensity of the contest for certain positions could point to links with organised crime, including the recruitment of hitmen and, in some cases, the direct involvement of criminal networks.

However, establishing the motive behind these killings is not always straightforward.

Rademeyer says some attacks that appear to be political assassinations could also be linked to other interests, including involvement in the taxi industry or illegal activities.

As the country approaches another local government election period, the links between political power, organised crime and targeted killings remain a concern.

World.title: NPA ready to defend Sibiya bail ruling if challenged
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) says it is prepared to defend the court’s decision to deny former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya bail if he challenges the ruling.

The Randburg Magistrate’s Court denied Sibiya bail on Tuesday. He faces charges of sexual grooming, human trafficking and the reckless handling of a firearm.

NPA spokesperson Kaizer Kganyago said the prosecution was confident in the evidence presented to the court and would oppose any appeal against the bail decision.

READ | Shadrack Sibiya denied bail

“We will always be ready to deal with whatever appeal it is. Justice has to be served in its totality, and if they feel that they need to appeal this matter, they can do so, and we will then come and defend,” Kganyago said.

“From where we are sitting as the NPA, we are comfortable that the evidence that we’ve put before the court is good enough, and that is why we got the ruling that we got today.”

READ | Sibiya rape accuser fears for her safety if he is granted bail

Kganyago also said the State was close to being ready for trial, with the investigating officer finalising outstanding work.

“We are just going to be tying up the last things the investigating officer is going to deal with, and we will be ready for trial, and we hope it can be done in a speedy manner,” he said.

Sibiya is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman and sexually grooming a 16-year-old girl. The allegations have not been proven in court.

World.title: Three police officers arrested at Polokwane airport
World.content:
POLOKWANE - Three police officers stationed at Polokwane International Airport have been arrested on charges of corruption and defeating the ends of justice.

According to Limpopo police, the investigation began approximately five months ago after information was received from members of the public.

The provincial police commissioner says the arrests send a strong message that corruption within the South African Police Service will not be tolerated.

However, authorities have not yet disclosed details of the specific allegations against the officers.

World.title: Threats of political violence soar in Australia's 'online echo chamber'
World.content:
SYDNEY - Australia's security chiefs had warned of "online echo chambers" fuelling grievances and conspiracies and stepped up prosecutions for threats of political violence ahead of Monday's attack on a lawmaker in a rural town.

Independent lawmaker Helen Haines, 65, underwent surgery overnight but remains in a critical condition after being struck deliberately by a car in an attack that "does shake all of us", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.

National broadcaster ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported she had lost a leg.

A man is in custody after Haines was hit outside her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres northeast of Melbourne.

Police described it as an isolated incident with the motive under investigation by the counter-terrorism team.

Acts of political violence are rare in Australia, and Albanese told the national broadcaster he wanted the country to remain a place where lawmakers can engage with people, go shopping, and watch football.

But he said security needed to be "dealt with" amid a significant increase in threats.

Australia's Human Rights Commission said the attack happened "against a backdrop of increasing polarisation and threats against politicians", which could undermine democracy.

Threats against Australian lawmakers and electorate offices doubled between 2021 and 2025, with 1,067 incidents reported to police last year.

The Australian Federal Police formed a National Security Investigations team last October, described by police commissioner Krissy Barrett as a "flying squad of hate disruptors", resulting in 41 people being charged for threats against federal politicians, ministers, and the prime minister.

Just this month, three men were charged by police over separate threats to politicians and government officials, and another three were sentenced by courts.

The nation's spy chief, Australian Security Intelligence Organisation director-general Mike Burgess, warned last year that politically motivated violence was among the agency's fastest-growing security concerns, driven by "grievance narratives, conspiracies and online echo chambers".

Political intolerance, violent rhetoric and polarisation were also contributing to a "permissive environment of violence", Burgess said on Tuesday.

Australia's Human Rights Commission said the attack happened "against a backdrop of increasing polarisation and threats against politicians" which could undermine democracy.

The lawmakers targeted are across the political spectrum and include men.

But the nature of threats directed at female lawmakers is "particularly troubling" because they are targeted because they are women, the federal police said last year.

The University of Melbourne's associate head of psychological sciences, Lisa Phillips, said she was not surprised it was a female lawmaker who had been attacked.

Victoria's state parliament commissioned Phillips to survey lawmakers on online abuse and stalking five years ago.

"The female politicians who responded almost ubiquitously reported experiences of either unwanted approaches, persistent unwanted contact from people, or experiences of threats or of assault," she told AFP.

Eighty-five percent of the threats received by the Victorian women lawmakers were gender-based abuse, the study found.

The attack on Haines may not be linked to federal politics, Phillips added.

"If you have a grievance against the system, you don't care which part of the system you are targeting."
