World.title: BJP’s delimitation gambit: Will it isolate Congress, puncture opposition’s SIR unity?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Is the government planning a new delimitation push to puncture the

âs bid to unite the opposition with protests against SIR? Union parliamentary affairs minister

has refuelled buzz that Parliament may be called for a short session to take up the legislation while also signalling Congressâs isolation on the issue by rejecting its demands for all-party consultations.

The government had tried to push through a Constitution Amendment Bill in April this year in Lok Sabha but failed. The proposed legislation, which aimed at implementing 33% reservation for women in legislatures from 2029 and increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats to 850 did not get the mandatory two-thirds majority. The bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against. It needed support of at least 352 out of the 528 members who were present and voted.

The Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026. It has been 68 days since then. However, the session is yet to be prorogued. This gap has broken the previous record of a 28-day delay for the Monsoon Session in 2015 and has left the opposition, especially the Congress, worried.

The Congress fears the government has been engaging in backroom moves with other parties in the opposition camp to cobble up a two-thirds majority and get the two Bills passed.





A look at how the number of seats may change based on estimates.

Kharge's missives to PM Modi

An anxious Congress president

has written four letters to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the last one four days ago. The Congress has been trying to pre-empt a sudden, surprise push by the government to pass the delimitation and womenâs reservation bills.

"You may kindly recall that I had first written to you on April 11, 2026, to convene an All-Party meeting before bringing any Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation.

You did not do so. Thereafter, you made the Bills public on the late evening of April 14, 2026 and convened a special session on April 16, 2026. The Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation failed to muster the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17, 2026, by a decisive margin," said Kharge in his letter.

"Thereafter, on July 16, 2026 and August 27, 2026, I wrote to you again, repeating our request for an All-Party meeting.

I am now doing so for a fourth time," the Congress chief said.

Kharge cautioned the government against taking a unilateral approach on major constitutional reforms such as national delimitation, which directly affects parliamentary constituency boundaries and regional representation.

Rijiju's sharp response to Kharge

In a sharp response to Kharge's Oct 16 letter to the Prime Minister, Rijiju said, "When after repeated requests Congress didn't give dates for discussion, govt's outreach extended to other political parties.

Consultations were held with representatives of parties including SP, DMK, YSRCP, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), AIMIM and BJD with a view to building a broader consensus in support of the proposed legislation.

"

Amit Shah dismissed concerns that delimitation would disadvantage southern states.

Rijiju also rejected Khargeâs concerns over the âunprecedentedâ delay in proroguing the Monsoon session. Dismissing Khargeâs contention, Rijiju cited precedents and underlined that no constitutional requirement existed prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die.

"The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety or irregularity," Rijiju said.

Why are opposition parties worried

When Parliament is adjourned sine die and not prorogued, it can be convened for a session at short notice. Sine die adjournment means that the session is suspended indefinitely without setting a day for reconvening. It does not mean a formal end of the session, which requires an official prorogation order by the President of India.

There is no specific timeframe for prorogation of Parliament after a session has been adjourned sine die.

But normally this happens within a few days.

Since the Delimitation Bill is a Constitution Amendment Bill and cannot be taken through an ordinance route it makes sense for the government to keep the option alive by not proroguing the session.

For the opposition, this is a clear signal that the government is still trying to get the numbers.

And that brings us to the second question of opposition unity.

The SIR unity vs Delimitation dilemma

The last few weeks have seen the opposition at its united best. The protests against SIR has seen the Congress not just reach out to but also accommodate every opposition party. There have been differences and some reports of one-upmanship, but by and large all parties have been together under the INDIA bloc. The DMK and AAP despite staying away from the opposition coalitionâs prorgrammes are united in the cause.

In fact, the DMK has sent mixed signals - supporting the agitation against NEET but also accusing the Congress of duplicity citing its support to VIjay and the TVK government in Tamil Nadu.

The AAP, on the other hand, has been active with the Cockroach Janata Party and has actively joined their protest programmes. Then there are parties which have been on both sides, like the Shiv Sena (UBT), Mamata Banerjee.

In fact, Naveen Patnaikâs Biju Janata Dal of Odisha that normally keeps equal distance from both the NDA and the INDIA bloc also joined one of the protests in Delhi to show solidarity with the cause.

And it's not just political parties; several civil society groups have also joined the INDIA bloc platform, amplifying the demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the reversal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has led to huge deletions of voters in several poll-bound states.

Interestingly, many political parties named by Kiren Rijiju in his statement have been part of the ongoing protests against SIR under the INDIA bloc.

Some that havenât joined the common protest have expressed solidarity with the cause and have protested separately.

This clearly poses a challenge to opposition unity. The Congress and many other opposition parties have been against the SIR and also the Delimitation Bill. However, while many of them are with the Congress on the issue of SIR, their independent negotiations with the government on the Delimitation Bill will keep the grand-old-party worried.

The BJP has reached out to several regional parties with an assurance that the proposed delimitation bill will not change the representation of states in Parliament, as the seats in Lok Sabha will be increased 50% across the states and not in proportion to the existing population as it should normally be under the delimitation process.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The BJP-led NDA governmentâs move to tag the womenâs reservation bill, which proposes to increase their representation in Lok Sabha, comes as an added pressure as well as incentive.

If the parties oppose, they are labelled as anti-women by the BJP and its ruling allies in their respective states. On the other hand, if they accept the proposal, they get the benefit of accommodating additional women without impacting the existing dominance of men.

Keen political contest

Clearly, this is going to be a keen contest between the BJP and the Congress. It will be interesting to see how the Congress manages to persuade its allies to stay united against BJPâs Delimitation plans. If some regional parties like the DMK, which are very unhappy with the Congress do decide to back the delimitation bill, will it take the sting out of the present SIR campaign?

The Congress, anyways, needs to realise that SIR cannot be the only glue that will hold together the opposition parties. The Supreme Court is already hearing a clutch of SIR related petitions. Also, the Election Commission has started the process re-enrolment of voters and also of SSR, the Special Summary revision of electoral rolls, in 14 states and 3 Union Territories. So, SIR as a unifying bond may not help the Congress for long.

The main opposition party needs to find lasting ways of ensuring that all its allies are united against the government.

World.title: No hacker, no warning: How AI agents can enter business systems without anyone noticing
World.content:
What if an AI agent being tested by a company on the other side of the world could quietly enter your businessâs systems, read confidential records and leave without triggering an alarm?

Indiaâs cybersecurity agency has flagged precisely this kind of risk, reporting cases in which AI agents accessed live systems during research and testing, exposing a blind spot in how companies protect their data from tools they may never have authorised.

In an advisory issued on October 15, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received voluntary disclosures from AI model providers whose agents had accessed live systems belonging to Indian organisations. The agents reportedly found their way in through exposed passwords, access keys left in public code repositories and cloud accounts with broader permissions than necessary.

The affected organisations did not detect the access themselves, CERT-In said. The incidents came to light through reviews by the AI developers, raising a troubling question: if an AI agent can cross into a real business system while being tested elsewhere, how would the business know what it had seen, or whether its data had been exposed?

Five security gaps that can expose businesses to AI agents

How can an AI test reach a real business?

AI agents are software systems that can carry out tasks with limited human involvement.

They can search the internet, use other software and make a series of decisions to complete a task.

Developers test these agents to understand what they can do. But if an agent is allowed to access the internet and comes across a working password or access key, it may be able to enter a system that was never meant to be part of the test.

For example, a company may accidentally leave an access key in a public code repository. If that key allows entry to a database, an AI agent that finds it may be able to read the information stored there.





Jaydeep Singh, general manager for India at cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, said an agent does not need hostile intent to cause a breach.

âIt needs a goal and valid access,â he said.

Singh said an agent may be given instructions to stay within a certain task, but those instructions cannot prevent access to other systems if its credentials allow it to go further.

Rajesh Chhabra, general manager for India and Asia at cybersecurity firm Acronis, said an agent may find credentials in a configuration file, code repository or cloud account that give it more access than its task requires.

âThe lesson isnât that the agent went rogue. It is that the permissions were weaker than anyone realised,â he said.

The disclosure does not establish that AI companies deliberately targeted Indian businesses. It does, however, raise questions about whether developers did enough to keep their tests separate from real business systems.

AI went looking online and found its way into Indian firmsâ confidential data

Why did the businesses not notice?

A company does not need to have an AI agent of its own for one to access its systems.

If an agent finds a working access key, it may be able to enter through the same channels used by employees and other software.

This can make the activity difficult to identify. Security systems may record that an account accessed a database, but not clearly show whether the account was being used by an employee, a software programme or an AI agent.

âLogs record the credential used, not whether a human, a script or an agent used it,â Singh said.

Some businesses also do not keep detailed records of which files or customer records were accessed after a successful login. Without these records, security teams may struggle to identify unusual activity.

Sunil Sharma, managing director and vice-president of sales for India and SAARC at cybersecurity firm Sophos, said agents can operate at machine speed while using valid credentials and broad access permissions.

âA legitimate agent can also become risky if it is compromised or misconfigured, so monitoring has to look at behaviour,â Sharma said. âThe principle is simple: trust the agentâs behaviour, not just its origin.â

Sophos' Active Adversary Report 2026, based on 661 incident response and managed detection cases handled between November 2024 and October 2025, found that 67 per cent of the investigated incidents involved identity-related attacks.

It also found that multi-factor authentication was missing in 59 per cent of cases and that gaps in the retention of security logs had doubled year on year.

These findings do not relate directly to the incidents disclosed by CERT-In. They point to wider problems with how organisations manage access to their systems and track activity within them.

CERT-In flags a new cyber blind spot

AI agents also raise risks for cyberattacks

CERT-In's advisory also described a separate set of incidents in which cybercriminals used AI tools to carry out attacks against Indian organisations.

The agency said these attacks reduced the time between gaining initial access to a system and causing damage from days to hours. It also observed that some organisations that had not fully addressed an earlier breach were attacked again on a larger scale.

The two situations are different. In the first, an AI agent under evaluation accessed systems beyond its authorised scope. In the second, criminals used AI tools to attack organisations.

Both show how quickly weaknesses such as exposed passwords and excessive access permissions can be exploited.

Kaspersky reported that its security products detected more than 92,000 attacks involving malware and potentially unwanted applications disguised as popular AI agents and services worldwide between January and early May 2026. It also identified more than 15,000 malware samples posing as agentic AI software, including fake versions of OpenClaw.

These figures concern malicious software disguised as AI tools, not the incidents reported by CERT-In. Read Kaspersky's findings.

Who is responsible if an AI agent accesses confidential data?

The CERT-In disclosure leaves an important question unanswered: when an AI company discovers that its model has accessed another organisation's data without permission, who must notify the affected business and help investigate what happened?

AI experiments spill into the real world

Manish Chasta, co-founder and chief technology officer of Eventus Security, said businesses investigating suspected access should examine records of logins, database activity, software requests and cloud access.

These records can help establish which account was used and what information it accessed.

If an access key is known to have been exposed, or there is credible evidence that it has been misused, it should be revoked or replaced promptly. Security teams should also check whether other accounts or access keys were created, while preserving records needed for the investigation.

CERT-In has recommended that AI developers restrict agents' internet access during testing, use fake credentials and test data instead of real business information, and monitor their activity.

Testing systems should be prevented from reaching unrelated live systems.

Businesses, meanwhile, should remove exposed access keys, review who can enter their systems and disable online services that are no longer needed.

Chhabra of Acronis said companies should test AI agents in a separate copy of their systems, using fake records and dummy credentials rather than putting live business data at risk.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The advisory does not establish how widespread these incidents are or whether the accessed data was transferred elsewhere.

But it shows how an AI test can affect a business that has no involvement in it.

For Indian organisations, the challenge is to detect when an account is being used in an unexpected way. For AI developers, it is to ensure that a model being tested cannot reach systems outside the approved environment. Neither should depend only on the AI following instructions.

World.title: Bhagwat warns protests can become political tools, urges restraint from govt too
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Warning that when a movement becomes âa tool of politicsâ, forces seeking to undermine India take advantage,

chief

on Tuesday linked political protests and distrust of institutions to alleged foreign attempts to destabilise the country.

But his Vijayadashami address in Nagpur also carried a message for governments: respect citizens' dignity, act within constitutional limits and avoid deepening divisions while addressing grievances.

The remarks came amid protests over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Bhagwat did not name the Commission, SIR or any political party, nor did he present evidence connecting the protests with foreign forces.

The warning was not new. In 2023, Bhagwat had identified âcultural Marxistsâ and âWokeâ forces as promoting anarchy through education, media and public discourse. In 2024, he invoked the âDeep Stateâ, alleging attempts to foster grievances and distrust of institutions. His 2025 Vijayadashami address warned against forces seeking to reproduce political upheavals witnessed in neighbouring countries.

What's different this year was the emphasis: instead of naming ideological adversaries, Bhagwat described their alleged methods, from deepening disagreements and cultivating a sense of victimhood to undermining faith in national institutions and drawing domestic political actors into the process.





Claiming that powers seeking to install proxies in other countries regarded India's rise as a threat, he said: âThey devise plans and work towards finding ways to dismantle Bharat, Hindu society, and Sangh.â Some ambitious political leaders, driven by âpetty political interestsâ, joined such efforts, he alleged, without identifying them.

Yet Bhagwat acknowledged the legitimacy of grievances. âIn our vast society problems do exist.

There are likely to be numerous shortcomings in the system as well. It is only natural that these may lead to agitations,â he said. âHowever, such agitations should aim to provide solutions.â

He applied that standard to protesters, political leaders and the state alike, asking them not to create âdiscord, animosity, resentment, bitterness, or divisionsâ. Even when emotions ran high, their actions should remain within the Constitution and law.

He warned that âthe lure of votes, cheap popularity, or political gainsâ must not overpower prudence and goodwill.

Earlier in the address, he specifically urged government officials implementing campaigns and policies to be courteous and considerate, and to respect citizens' dignity. âExperience shows that it is neither the government alone that can resolve all the problems of society, nor is it true that problems can be resolved only through agitations,â he said, advocating dialogue and community participation.

That theme opened into the RSS's post-centenary plans. Bhagwat said Swayamsevaks would work to bring together organisations combating drug addiction and build nationwide resistance to what he called a âserious national problemâ. He also urged the government to consider restrictions on OTT platforms, while asking families to teach young people to distinguish appropriate from inappropriate digital content.

Although concerns over drugs and digital content had figured in his 2024 address too, the proposed nationwide mobilisation gave the anti-drug initiative a more specific organisational direction.

In education, he cited observations from around 1,296 rural schools across 210 districts in 21 Sangh organisational regions, claiming improvements in attendance, learning and parental involvement where Swayamsevaks and villagers cooperated.

No underlying methodology was disclosed in the speech.

Bhagwat said centenary outreach had covered over 10 crore households in 4.61 lakh villages and 41,076 urban localities. Contacts at home and abroad would continue, he indicated. The organisation's five initiatives â social harmony, family awareness, environment, self-awareness and Swadeshi, and civic discipline â were ânot merely programs to be undertaken for a yearâ, but intended to change everyday conduct.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

On identity, Bhagwat said the Hindu worldview prescribed no particular form of worship, food habit, language or caste, and called for acceptance of diversity within shared national belonging. He also advocated singing 'Vande Mataram' in full, entering a dispute in which Congress has reaffirmed its decision to sing only the first two stanzas at party events.

The address thus combined a familiar warning about alleged external interference with a stronger appeal for constitutional restraint and a continuing society-led role for the RSS beyond its centenary.

World.title: Special trains between Thiruvananthapuram North and Mangaluru on October 20th and 21st
World.content:
South Western Railway will operate one trip each of an express special train in both directions between Thiruvananthapuram North and Mangaluru Junction to clear the extra rush of passengers during the festival season.

Train No. 06155 will leave Thiruvananthapuram North at 7.40 p.m. on October 20 and reach Mangaluru Junction at 9 a.m. the next day.

The return service, Train No. 06156, will leave Mangaluru Junction at 10.15 a.m. on October 21 and arrive at Thiruvananthapuram North at 11.45 p.m. the same day.

The trains will stop at Varkala Sivagiri, Kollam Junction, Kayamkulam Junction, Alappuzha, Cherthala, Ernakulam Junction, Aluva, Thrissur, Shoranur Junction, Tirur, Kozhikode, Vadakara, Thalassery, Kannur, Payyanur, Kanhangad and Kasaragod. Passengers have been requested to make use of the special services.

World.title: Four arrested for multiple thefts
World.content:
The police have arrested four persons who were allegedly involved in multiple thefts, mainly targeting grocery and petty shops in different parts of Coimbatore.

The arrested have been identified as Ayyaz Mohammed (19) of Kottaimedu at Ukkadam, M. Muhseen (19) of Kallamedu at Selvapuram, J. Jaseel (20) and R. Sahabudin (19) of Karumbukadai at Ukkadam.

According to the police, a series of thefts targeting grocery and small shops were reported in Kinathukadavu recently. Cash and cartons of cigarettes were primarily reported stolen from the shops.

The police examined surveillance cameras and found four persons gaining entry into shops for theft. Investigations by the police revealed that Mohammed, Muhseen, Jaseel and Sahabudin were involved in the thefts. Three of the accused were arrested by Annur police while one was arrested by the Kinathukadavu police.

The police stated that alleged involvement of the four persons in multiple thefts reported in different parts of Coimbatore was being investigated.

World.title: Dussehra 2026: Traffic curbs in Dwarka, security tightened in Delhi-NCR and more
World.content:
In view of the Dussehra celebrations, security has been tightened around Delhi-NCR area, while the traffic police have issued advisory on the roads that are likely to be affected on Tuesday (October 20, 2026).

Traffic restrictions may be imposed in Dwarka and parts of South Delhi, the police have said.

Traffic curbs in Dwarka

The Delhi Traffic Police have issued an advisory, pointing out that restrictions may be imposed on six roads in Dwarka on Tuesday (October 20) evening. This is in view of the heavy pedestrian and vehicular movement expected due to a large gathering and anticipated VVIP movement.

Which are the roads likely to be affected in Dwarka

The restrictions will be in place from 4.50 p.m. to 8 p.m. on

UER-II

Dwarka Expressway

Roads No. 224, 226, 203 and 205

Commuters have been advised to avoid these roads, if possible, and take alternative routes, the advisory said.

Ravana Dahan in Dwarka

A 221-foot-tall effigy of Ravana is set to be burnt at Sector 10 in Dwarka on Vijayadashami, with the Dwarka Shri Ramlila Society announcing it as one of the tallest Ravana effigies in the country for the 2026 Dussehra celebrations.

Dussehra celebrations at Red Fort

In view of the Dussehra celebrations at Red Fort, the Delhi Traffic Police have said that traffic restrictions and parking regulations will be imposed from 3 p.m. to 11 p.m. on October 20. As per the advisory, traffic movement on Netaji Subhash Marg and Nishad Raj Marg may be restricted or regulated depending on prevailing traffic conditions and security requirements.

Which are the areas likely to be affected

Chhatta Rail Chowk

Delhi Gate

Shanti Van Chowk

GPO Chowk

Parade Ground Parking

More than 13,000 police personnel will be deployed across Delhi-NCR to ensure tight security during Dussehra celebrations, with heightened vigilance at religious sites and places expected to see large public gatherings, officers said.

As per a PTI report, around 2,200 police personnel have been deployed at 66 ‘Ravan Dahan’ sites, 17 religious processions and other related events in Gurugram. Elaborate security arrangements with 1,200 police personnel have also been made in Faridabad to maintain law and order.

World.title: Transport Minister inspects special buses in Salem
World.content:
Transport Minister A. Vijay Tamilan Parthiban inspected special buses operated to clear the festive rush at the Salem New Bus Stand on Tuesday (October 20, 2026), following the end of Ayudha pooja holidays.

To clear the rush at the bus stand, special buses to Chennai are operating for two days on Tuesday and Wednesday (October 21) at the Corporation vacant land near the New Bus Stand.

The Minister inspected the bus stand premises along with the officials and interacted with the passengers waiting at the bus stand. He came across elderly persons living on the bus stand premises and instructed officials to enrol them into old age homes. The Minister also inspected the toilets and instructed officials to keep it clean.

The Minister noticed that the fans and chairs installed at the bus stand were missing. He asked for details about the missing items and instructed that the fans at the bus stand be operated.

Later, he went to Manalmedu TMS Bus Stop and interacted with the people there. Some travellers alleged that buses did not pick up passengers at the bus stop, so the Minister stopped the bus and instructed them to pick up passengers at the bus stop.

World.title: From death row to award-winning author, C. Selvam expresses remorse, reflects on the families of his victims
World.content:
Oru Thooku Kaithiyin Vaakumoolam, a prison memoir by death-row convict C. Selvam, is a testament to the transformative power of reading, even on a mind hardened by violence.

“I started reading in the early years of my prison life. But I turned my attention to serious literature and novels after we were sentenced to death. Reading serious literature is different from reading ordinary books. I can read 400 pages of ordinary books, but only 200 pages of serious literature,” said Mr. Selvam, whose book has been selected for the Iyal Award, which is instituted by the Canada-based Tamil Literary Garden. The award was presented to him in absentia on October 18, 2026.

Mr. Selvam and his two associates, Sheik Meeran and Radhakrishnan, were sentenced to death for murdering Ayyavu, a notorious gangster, inside a court in Nagercoil in 1994. Though their death sentences were later commuted to life imprisonment, they would have to spend the rest of their lives in prison. They have already completed 32 years behind bars.

A rivalry turned violent

The murder was an act of revenge. The rivalry turned violent after Ayyavu and his associates killed 17 cows belonging to Mr. Selvam’s family in Puthukudiyiruppu, one of the most feared areas of Kanniyakumari district, after failing to find him. Enraged, Mr. Selvam and his friends retaliated by killing Ayyavu inside the Nagercoil court. The incident sent shockwaves across the State.

“I have the blood of the past on my hands. Nowhere in the book have I claimed that I am innocent or that false cases were foisted on me. The period, the place I lived in, the politics of the day, the circumstances, and my age would all have played a role in the tragedies. But I hope I have become a good man,” he told The Hindu ahead of the award ceremony.

“Oh, people living in the light, I take you to a world surrounded by darkness. Only sharp eyesight can spot the light in that dark world, but not its heat.”

Thus begins Mr. Selvam’s introduction to his chilling account. The manuscript, written in his neat handwriting, is still in his possession. The maturity of his language, both spoken and written, and the change in his outlook speak volumes about the transformative power of sustained reading.

‘Overcome by emotion’

After marrying and starting a family, Mr. Selvam said, he was overcome by emotion whenever he thought of the families of those who had been killed. “When I think of buying sweets and new clothes for my children during festivals, my thoughts inevitably turn to the children of the dead. Of course, their mothers would provide for them. But nothing can compensate for the absence of a father. Just think of how much a family suffers when it loses its father. The thought has plunged me into depression,” he said, his voice breaking with emotion.

Mr. Selvam, who surrendered to the police in 1994, began by reading small books, particularly those on Periyar, the founder of the Dravidar Kazhagam, and his works. Fellow inmates, including Mukilan and Pozhilan, who were detained for their political activities and affiliations, introduced him to the world of books.

“But I never imagined that books would reshape my thinking and reconstruct my personality. I had heard about the healing and transformative power of books. Today, however, I stand before you as an example,” said Mr. Selvam, who had not studied beyond Class VIII.

It was in 1998, after his death sentence was confirmed, that he plunged headlong into serious literature and fiction by the great masters. Egged on by Mukilan, an activist who was at the forefront of protests against Sterlite and other campaigns, Mr. Selvam began writing, albeit half-heartedly. He received further encouragement from writer and scholar S.V. Rajadurai.

“I began writing in 2019 with a pen and notebook given to me by Mukilan. I completed 45 pages in a day, and Mukilan appreciated my effort,” Mr. Selvam said, recalling his journey as a writer. Publisher Badri Seshadri, who met Selvam by chance at Tiruchi prison, was impressed by his writing. His publishing house, Kizhakku Pathippagam, subsequently published the book.

When told that his book could become one of the finest works of prison literature, Mr. Selvam smiled and asked, “Have you read the prison memoir of the late communist leader K. Baladhandayutham? In my opinion, it is the best book.”

World.title: CJP seeks urgent hearing in Delhi High Court challenging judicial custody of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
World.content:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) moved the Delhi High Court for an urgent hearing over the extension of the judicial custody of its leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das.

“We have moved the Delhi High Court and requested an urgent night hearing. Saurav and Ashutosh should not spend a single minute behind bars. Their liberty must not be curtailed because of political games,” Ratna Singh, CJP’s legal head, said in a post on X. The CJP has sought a night hearing in the Delhi High Court, which is shut this week due to Dasara.

We have moved the Delhi High Court and requested an urgent night hearing. Saurav and Ashutosh should not spend a single minute behind bars. Their liberty must not be curtailed because of political games. Justice must not wait. @Cockroachisback — Ratna Singh (@whattalawyer) October 20, 2026

A newly-appointed Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg police station on Monday (October 19, 2026) ordered Mr. Das’s and Mr. Ranka’s judicial remand for two more days after they were produced before him. The two leaders were taken into custody on October 13 after they allegedly climbed over a locked gate to enter Jantar Mantar, which had earlier been denotified as a designated protest site, and were sent to five-day judicial custody initially.

The CJP has alleged that the bail proceedings in the case have been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its leaders. Along with other CJP workers, Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka displayed the national flag at the site and shouted slogans against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar before being detained and placed under preventive arrest.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Marco Rubio to skip Delhi, visit Mumbai and Jamnagar next week
World.content:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India for his second visit in six months, with energy and trade relations at the top of the agenda as he visits Mumbai and Jamnagar, the U.S. Department of State announced on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).

However, Mr. Rubio, who is expected to visit India from October 19 to 22 after travelling to Samarkand in Uzbekistan for a regional conference, will skip Delhi.

“[Mr. Rubio] will meet with senior government officials to strengthen the U.S.-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation,” the State department said in the statement, adding that Mr. Rubio will also meet business leaders to “promote investment opportunities”.

Mr. Rubio’s scheduled visit to Jamnagar is important as it hosts the world’s largest single-site refinery, operated by Reliance industries, and is expected to include a major reception hosted by the Ambani family. The Jamnagar refinery is one of the top three companies refining Russian Ural crude oil, although it has reduced its share of the imports. The visit would follow just a day after U.S. President Donald Trump is mandated by the U.S. Congress to propose extra tariffs as sanctions on India and other countries buying Russian oil, under the Sanctions Against Russian and Iran Act (SRIA) passed into law last month.

In March 2026, Mr. Trump announced that Reliance Industries would invest in a refinery in Brownsville, Texas, although details of the exact collaboration have still not been released.

The U.S. Secretary of State is expected to meet External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar during the visit, but the Ministry of External Affairs didn’t confirm the visit or answer questions on why Mr. Rubio is skipping Delhi on this visit.

Asked about the U.S. statement on the trip, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the government would make the announcement “at the appropriate time as to what will be the issues to be taken up”. He also said that the government would disclose details of the visit “as and when they happen”. To another question, he said that India had already conveyed its concerns over the SRIA to the U.S. government.

Tension in ties

The visit by Mr. Rubio comes at a time of tensions in the India-U.S. economic relationship for a number of other reasons as well. Senior officials and Ministers on both sides have acknowledged there is trouble in the Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA), with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman saying that the talks last week had “plateaued”.

The U.S.-India ties were dealt another blow last week as the Trump administration suspended permission for five Indian tech outsourcing companies to certify Indian professionals as eligible for green cards or permanent residency. The visit would also come just ahead of the key mid-term elections in the U.S., where Mr. Trump’s Republican Party is expected to face losses.

Mr. Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi are due to meet nonetheless on December 13, on the sidelines of the G20 summit in Florida, and possibly in November at the ASEAN linked summits in Manila. Both leaders spoke over the telephone on September 30.

In Kolkata on Monday for celebrations of the U.S.’s 250th Independence day anniversary, U.S. Ambassador to India and the region Sergio Gor indicated to journalists that more engagements would be announced soon, saying “stay tuned for what comes next.” Mr. Rubio last visited Delhi in May 2026 to attend the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting.
